item.title: What is the Rutgers quarterback situation entering Michigan game?
item.description: PISCATAWAY – In a season filled with quarterback questions, now Rutgers football is facing another . Who will start this week’s game against Michigan? That’s the newest question and it’s relevant after starter Dylan Lonergan suffered an injury early in the Scarlet Knights ’ 42-14 loss to Northwestern on Oct. 24, and whether he’ll be able to play remains unclear. Schiano said Tuesday, Oct. 27 that he will leave Lonergan’s status to the availability report, the first of which is released Wednesday night. It was the second game this season that Lonergan had to leave because of an injury – he also missed the team’s game against Boston College (the second game of the season) because of the injury he suffered in Week 1 in the loss to UMass. It’s been a disappointing campaign so far for Lonergan, who was showing signs of improvement and played his best game as a Scarlet Knight in the Oct. 17 win over Maryland. “I’m disappointed and sad for the kid because this means so much to him and he puts so much of himself into it,” Schiano said. “To have to leave the game now for the (second) time, yeah it’s killing him. And I’m sad for us because he really was coming on. You could see it against (Southern California) and you could see it at Maryland. You could see him really coming on. Injuries are part of football. It’s a violent game.” If Lonergan can’t play, then Rutgers has to look to AJ Surace or Sean Ashenfelder. Surace again struggled after coming in for Lonergan, going just 7-of-18 passing for 64 yards with one interception against Northwestern. Seeking a spark in the second half, Schiano called on third-stringer Sean Ashenfelder, who went 2-of-9 for 36 yards. Ashenfelder hasn’t even gotten many practice reps, partially because the bulk of them in even in training camp went to Lonergan and Surace as they battled for the job. Schiano reiterated again Tuesday that once the season starts, there are even fewer reps to go around. Surace is in his third year with the program and he just hasn’t played well enough in the chances he’s gotten so far this season. Schiano, though, has liked how Surace has battled through the adversity. He’s still confident in Surace’s ability. “AJ’s a fighter,” Schiano said. “He’s not happy with the way he’s played. But he came out in practice like the national championship’s around the corner. That’s the way he approaches everything he does. If you’re going to bet on a guy, probably bet on him.” This article originally appeared on Asbury Park Press: What is the Rutgers quarterback situation entering Michigan game?

item.title: Enduring memories and 'imposter syndrome' - The GAA Social meets Mayo star Carney
item.description: Jack Carney's inspirational displays in the Mayo midfield has earned him a Footballer of the Year nomination [Getty Images] Jack Carney has two enduring memories from the whirlwind of celebrations that followed Mayo's return to the promised land after 75 years. Both are linked to places that helped shape him. He will never forget seeing the crowd of people that waited at Kilmeena - his home club - to see their heroes bring Sam Maguire onto their patch. Kilmeena was the last stop on the All-Ireland champions' homecoming parade, as Andy Moran's side were roared Running behind schedule, when the bus finally arrived, Carney was struck by the numbers that stuck around to see one of their own. "To see the amount of people that waited there just to see the team, to see Sam Maguire returning to such a small club, no-one ever thought it was possible," Carney tells Thomas Niblock and Oisin McConville on the GAA Social. "To finally bring it back there to my local people was something I'll never forget." Jack Carney- Winning the All-Ireland with Mayo 'This is something different here' The other memory Carney hopes proves ineradicable is the powerful feeling that accompanied carrying Sam onto Achill Island alongside team-mates Donnacha McHugh and Diarmuid O'Connor. Carney has deep family roots on the island. His father and grandfather hail from there and both were present as Carney, McHugh and O'Connor - soundtracked by more than 100 bagpipers, including his father - carried the famous trophy across the Michael Davitt Bridge and onto the island. Given his connection to Achill, the power and significance of the moment was not lost on Carney. "According to my father and grandfather, that's never happened before [bringing Sam Maguire on to the island], so I recognised the cultural importance of it - and you could feel it," says Carney. "That originally wasn't on the calendar as a club until further down the line. The island empties when summer is over. People return to where they're from originally, Dublin or Galway or wherever, and I really wanted to get the trophy down there while the island was vibrant and alive. "My grandfather was the sergeant on Achill Island. My father grew up in the barracks and the GAA pitch was the back garden. They kind of claim me as half one of their own." Carney, whose two-point score launched Mayo's All-Ireland final comeback against Kerry, added: "With no Achill player on the team, it was really important that both myself and Donnacha - both our fathers are from there - to get down there and show our appreciation for what they've done for us and our families. "And Diarmuid O'Connor just has a sense of knowing when something will be good and when to be there. "He came down with us and I'm delighted he was there because someone who didn't really understand the weight of it all - when we were crossing the bridge, he could say he could just feel it, he said, 'this is something different here'." Carney kicked a couple of two-pointers

item.title: Vote for the Savannah Morning News Athlete of the Week in an open poll
item.description: There were some memorable individual performances last week in the Savannah high school sports scene. Myla Shippy of Savannah Christian slammed home 17 kills to lead the Raiders over Holy Innocents and into the state semifinals for the first time since 2016. Ellie Ayala of Savannah Arts was all over the court for the Panther volleyball team in an impressive road win at Amuchee as the Panthers reached the state semifinals for the fourth year in a row. Stanley Smart Jr. had a career-high four touchdown runs in a win over Wayne County and Windsor Forest quarterback Jayden Martin did it all in an overtime win over Harlem. This is a chance for readers to weigh in and select the Savannah Morning News High School Athlete of the Week in an open poll with no restrictions on the voting. The poll will close at 11 a.m. on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Here are the candidates. Stanley Smart Jr., Benedictine The senior ran for 82 yards on nine carries and scored a career-high four touchdowns in a win over Wayne County. Myla Shippy, Savannah Christian The junior had 17 kills, 15 digs, two aces and 24 serves received as Savannah Christian swept Holy Innoncents to advance to the Private School State semifinals for the first time since 2016. Jayden Martin, Windsor Forest The junior was 16 of 26 passing for 160 yards and two touchdowns and ran for 45 yards and two scores on 13 carries and caught the game-winning pass from Kamari Duncan on a trick-play two-point conversion in overtime to lead the Knights to a 29-28 win over Harlem. Ellie Ayala, Savannah Arts The junior had 12 kills, four aces, 20 digs and 17 assists as the Panthers went on the road to beat Amuchee three sets to one in a Class A/AA quarterfinal. Jah'Barri Felix, Bradwell The senior was 17-for-20 passing for 304 yards with three touchdowns and an interception and ran for 32 yards and a pair of scores on three carries in a win over Lakeside-Evans. Gessilyn Clark, Richmond Hill The junior earned the complete game victory in a 4-2 win over Dacula in a deciding Game 3 of the Class 7A State Softball quarterfinals. She has thrown five complete games in the playoffs with a 4-1 record. Tamiya Washington, Groves The senior quarterback was 15 of 21 passing for three touchdowns and ran for 67 yards and a pair of scores in a win over Savannah Arts. James Mobley IV, Calvary Day The senior was 9 of 11 passing for 142 yards and three touchdowns and recorded his 100th career touchdown pass on a toss to Jalen Hicks, who made his 100th career reception on the catch, in a win over Savannah High. Kendall Ward, South Effingham The freshman went 3 for 4 with a home run and four RBIs and earned the win in the pitching circle as the Mustangs beat Coffee to sweep the series and advance to the Class 6A Elite Eight. Matthew Dillon, Effingham County The sophomore was 8 of 11 for 182 yards and three touchdowns in a win over Grovetown. item.title: Twenty-seven WASC swimmers combine for 57 first-place finishes in meet
item.description: WATERTOWN — The Watertown Area Swim Club Dolphins kicked off what they hope will be another very successful short-course season in 2026-27 by hosting the Ghouls in the Pool meet. The one-day meet was held on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026, in the Prairie Lakes Wellness Center's indoor pool. The home meet was the first of four scheduled home meets this season for the Dolphins , who have finished second in the State Class A Short-Course Championships each of the past 10 years and second in the State Class A Long-Course Championships eight years in a row. Watertown also has regular-season meets scheduled at the PLWC on Dec. 4-6 (2026), Jan. 16-17 (2027) and Feb. 5-7 (2027) before hosting the State Class A 12-and-Under Championships on Feb. 26-28 (2027). The State Class A 13-and-Under Championships are slated for March 4-7 (2027) at Pierre. WASC Girls Fourteen female swimmers combined for 29 first-place events in the Ghouls in the Pool meet. Collins DeBoer (ages 11-12), Marie Makens (6-and-under) and Sydney Sparks (17-19) each won four races. Charlotte Holien (13-14) and Haevyn Jones (13-14) each won three races and Amelia Erickson (9-10) and Essence Hinkelman (11-12) each two. Other event winners were Gracie Anderson (11-12), Everlie Fischbach (13-14), Justine Kranz (15-16), McKenzie McKeever (7-8), Harper Meidinger (17-19), Josephine Waite (15-16) and Jada Leigh Wellnitz (15-16). WASC Boys Thirteen male swimmers produced 28 first-place finishes for the Dolphins. Leading the way for WASC was Griffen Gerrish (6-and-under) with four wins and Flynn Erickson (7-8), Clayton Muller (13-14) and Cooper Smith (15-16) with three apiece. Paul Feist (17-19), Owen Hoots (9-10), Pierce Mathiason (17-19), RJ Matthies (15-16), Brooks Melmer (7-8) and Kuper Simons (13-14) each won two races and Channing DeBoer (13-14), Rhett Ellingson (7-8), and Penn Feist (15-16) each one. Complete WASC's results from Sunday's meet are posted online at www.thepublicopinion.com . Follow Watertown Public Opinion sports reporter Roger Merriam on X (formerly known as Twitter) @PO_Sports or email: rmerriam@thepublicopinion.com This article originally appeared on Watertown Public Opinion: Twenty-seven WASC swimmers combine for 57 first-place finishes in meet

item.title: Fennville's mother-daughters combo connects championship volleyball teams
item.description: FENNVILLE - When Morgan Winne played volleyball for Fennville High School, the team was strong. The Blackhawks won the SAC conference title in 2000 and 2001, winning a district championship in the latter. "It started in 2000. We had a really good team and won conference my junior and senior year. We had really good chemistry and won districts in 2001 as well. We want to strive for that this year, too," Winne said. "We have been trying to build that culture back up and we are on an upward trajectory." That trajectory has been fun for the Winne family as Morgan Winne is an assistant coach with daughters Marynn and Adelynn on the team. More: Fennville volleyball claims first SAC division title since 2001 with huge sweep More: Fennville's MacKenzie McIlwain reached unprecedented milestones no one in area history has reached "It has been really fun to see them come out of their shells and just gain confidence throughout the season," Morgan Winne said. "It is really special to have them experience what I did 25 years ago." The next generation of Winnes understand how special this opportunity is, especially with their mom getting to share in the journey. "She has been there for me and my sister, supporting us," Marynn said. "Us being together definitely creates a stronger bond." There are, of course, struggles and challenges with having a mom for a coach - and a sister for a teammate. "We definitely argue a lot because we are siblings, but that also makes us stronger. We have a strong energy together on the court," Adelynn said. "It is definitely nostalgic for her and she has helped us understand what it takes to get here. "It is challenging to be a mom and a coach. You feel like you need to be tougher on your own kids. It is hard to separate that boundary and find the balance," Morgan said. "It is very exciting to see all the hard work. We have always known it has been possible and to have them taste what it is like to win, they are understanding their potential. It is really fun to see, especially with my two girls on the team." The Blackhawks will have all three Winnes together again next year as they look to keep the momentum of the program upswing going. "It means a lot to us. We knew it was a possibility but we had to work hard and work together to get it," Marynn said. "It definitely gives us a boost for the years to come, knowing what it takes to win conference." Contact sports editor Dan D’Addona at Dan.D’Addona@hollandsentinel.com. Follow him on X, formerly known as Twitter @DanDAddona or Facebook @HollandSentinelSport s. item.title: FIA partners with AWS to help drive future F1 regulations
item.description: Motorsport photo The FIA has announced a wide-ranging partnership with Amazon Web Services as it aims to upgrade its digital capabilities. AWS will join as its Official AI and Cloud Computing Partner, as the governing body will use AWS's suite of AI tools to improve its capability to produce future technical regulations. The FIA also runs its aerodynamic simulations on AWS’s High Performance Computing technology, allowing it to conduct air flow tests in the virtual world without having to build physical parts, speeding up the process and reducing the costs involved. This partnership also expands the digital licensing platform the governing body uses to simplify tasks like licence administration, which should make it easier for national sporting authorities to run their events and for officials to sign up. That digital platform, first trialled in Canada and Sri Lanka, will now be rolled out across more countries. Sepang race start Sepang race start The AWS integration forms part of the FIA’s wider digital transformation, as president Mohammed Ben Sulayem explained. "Technology is changing every part of our sport, and the FIA must lead that change. Our new partnership with AWS will support everything from the cars of the future to the grassroots clubs where so many careers begin. "By bringing world-class cloud and AI technology into the heart of the FIA, we can make it simpler for drivers, officials and volunteers to take part, help our Member Clubs work more efficiently, and move closer to our ambition of doubling global motor sport participation." AWS is already an existing partner of F1 management, having joined in 2018 as its innovation technology partner. Among other services, AWS tools process telemetry data for broadcast use, powering live strategy predictions. item.title: Liverpool may be sleepwalking into diabolical 2027 transfer mistake – opinion
item.description: Liverpool may be sleepwalking into diabolical 2027 transfer mistake – opinion Jose Mourinho is reportedly keen on Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister. Sky Sports Germany claim that the Argentine star is high on Real Madrid’s wishlist, with the Spanish outfit paying close attention to the situation ahead of the footballer’s contract expiring in the summer of 2028. On current evidence, Liverpool should keep Alexis Mac Allister (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) There were suspicions that a truly horrendous domestic campaign from the former Brighton man would culminate in his departure from Anfield this summer. However, following an impressive (and evidently rejuvenating) World Cup campaign with Argentina, we’ve seen Mac Allister reborn in the middle of the park for Andoni Iraola’s men . In fact, there’s a pretty convincing case you could make for the 27-year-old being a strong contender, alongside Jeremy Jacquet, for Liverpool’s player of the season, as things currently stand. There were serious concerns about the midfielder’s legs being gone, given he’s endured a relentless run of fixtures between his involvement across Brighton, Liverpool and the national side. But if we’re seeing this version of Alexis Mac Allister every week, and there’s hope for some longevity beyond the end of his contract, you have to wonder whether Liverpool might be tempted to extend his current terms – even if only to protect his value. The case for selling Mac Allister to Real Madrid (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Reporting from Sky Sports Switzerland claims that Liverpool are firm on the idea that they won’t be offering their leading performer a contract extension, despite Mac Allister being more than open to extending his stay at L4. Why? Well, the Reds are reportedly planning another midfield overhaul, and so Mac Allister is presumably one name that could be sacrificed on the transfer pyre in the interest of bringing in a quality signing. There is some sense in this approach; the former Seagulls man is, currently, one of our more valuable assets. But if you’re selling a player with a year left on his contract, you’re opening yourself to being bullied on the price tag (if you’re not prepared to risk a free exit) without a bidding war, and it seems like Real Madrid are the only really keen suitors at this stage. But, realistically, what are Liverpool hoping to achieve with this? Because on current evidence, Alexis Mac Allister is the one senior midfielder who appears to have taken to Andoni Iraola’s methods like a duck to water. He sits deeper than Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, and his passing is considerably more impactful – is there an expectation that either of his teammates will improve in that regard? We all broadly agree that bringing in a more natural six would be a sound move for the recruitment team. But would selling the Argentina international really be in our best interests? We’re going to need to see some serious improvement from Szobo

item.title: Preview | Austria Wien vs Juventus Women | UWCL
item.description: Preview | Austria Wien vs Juventus Women | UWCL The UEFA Women's Champions League is back, and the Women's First Team are heading to Austria to take on Austria Wien on Matchday 3 of the League Phase. Isaac Guerrero's side lost their opening UWCL game 2-1 against Benfica. but won 3-0 away at Hacken to get the campaign off the mark on Matchday 2. Let’s get up to speed ahead of the game with the pre-match stats. INTERESTING FACTS The meeting between Austria Wien and Juventus will be their first-ever UEFA Women's Champions League match; overall, Italian teams are unbeaten against Austrian sides in the competition (W8, D3). Juventus are unbeaten in their last four UEFA Women's Champions League away games (W3, D1) after losing three in a row previously; the Bianconere's biggest away win in the competition came in their only previous meeting in Austria (5-0 against St. Pölten in December 2025). Juventus has the third-most recoveries from pressing situations in the UWCL this season (33, behind only Arsenal and Barcelona). Alba Redondo of Juventus has attempted the most shots of any player in this UEFA Women's Champions League season (14) and has scored in both of her matches in the tournament. Alba Redondo has been directly involved in 12 of Juventus' 28 goals this season, across all competitions, with nine goals and three assists (43%). UWCL | BK Häcken-Juventus Women | Gallery OPPOSITION FOCUS Austria Wien are yet to win after their first two UEFA Women's Champions League matches (D1, L1); however, they picked up their first-ever points in the competition on Matchday 2 against Italian opposition (1-1 against Inter). No team has had more different players score than Austria Wien in the 2026/27 Austrian Championship: 11 in 10 matches played, the same as St. Pölten. Among the 221 players to have attempted 25 or more passes in the 2026/27 UEFA Women's Champions League, Jasmin Pal of Austria Wien boasts the highest percentage of forward passes (78%, 53 out of 68).

item.title: Rare Debut Win For Red Wings Homegrown Goalie
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The performance by Detroit Red Wings goalie Michal Postava in his first NHL start, as he downed Connor McDavid and the Edmonton Oilers on the road was impressive. “Postava, we’re so excited for him and happy for him,” Red Wings coach Todd McLellan told reporters after the game. “Sometimes that’s how it happens. A goalie gets a start such as this one and plays really well and gets the win. YOU ALREADY KNOW🦺 pic.twitter.com/fznL5avMvq — Detroit Red Wings (@DetroitRedWings) October 27, 2026 It was also rare. Since 1990, only 12 homegrown goalies have made their NHL debut between the posts for the Red Wings. Postava was just the fifth among that group to earn the win in his first NHL start. He’s just the third Detroit goalie to do so since 2005. The Red Wings have seen a bright future ahead for Postava since they signed him as an undrafted free agent in the summer of 2025. He was stalwart and consistent last season with the AHL Grand Rapids Griffins . Postava took things up another notch in his stinginess so far this season. When he was called up, Cossa was 4-0 with a 1.25 GAA and .954 save percentage for the Griffins. “He may be smaller than some of the monsters that are in the league right now, but he is very athletic,” McLellan said. “We think that he anticipates so well he can read where the shot release is going. He gets into position, and then there’s not a lot that lays around after.” CINEMA pic.twitter.com/2tq9NfFCkl — Detroit Red Wings (@DetroitRedWings) October 27, 2026 In the win, Postava stopped all three shots he faced in the shootout, including the one from NHL scoring leader McDavid. “Yeah, it’s crazy,” Postava told reporters. “Like, he’s one of the best players that ever played. And I’m just happy now and don’t have words.” Red Wings Not Known For Growing Their Own Goalies Historically, the Red Wings are big spenders when it comes to goalies. They sign UFAs. They trade for high-end talent. Homegrown puckstoppers are few and far between in Hockeytown. Postava is the first one to make his first NHL start for Detroit since Jared Coreau. On December 3, 2016, Coreau suffered a 5-3 loss to the Pittsburgh Penguins. Postava is the first Red Wings goalie to win his first NHL start in a Detroit uniform since fellow Czech goalie Petr Mrazek beat the St. Louis Blues 5-1 on February 7, 2013. Jimmy Howard (Nov. 28, 2005, 5-2 win vs. the Los Angeles Kings), Norm Maracle (March 17, 1996, 4-3 win vs. Edmonton) and Kevin Hodson (January 6, 1996, 3-0 win vs. the Chicago Blackhawks) also were winners when they made their first NHL start for the Red Wings. Chris Osgood and the Red Wings fell 6-3 to the Toronto Maple Leafs on October 15, 1993, in his first NHL start. Scott King got his first NHL start for the Red Wings on January 28, 1991, against the New Jersey Devils. He didn’t figure in the decision as Detroit lost 6-2. Sebastian Cossa (December 9, 2024 vs. the Buffalo Sabres), Tom McCollum (March 30, 2011 vs. St. Louis)

item.title: Dani Carvajal opens up on Real Madrid exit, Valverde, Ancelotti, El Clasico, future return
item.description: Dani Carvajal opens up on Real Madrid exit, Valverde, Ancelotti, El Clasico, future return Dani Carvajal is adjusting to life away from Real Madrid after spending 23 years associated with the club, but his emotional connection to the Bernabeu remains strong. In an interview with AS , the former Madrid defender reflected on his departure, praised Federico Valverde’s performances and identified Carlo Ancelotti as the manager who had the greatest influence on his career. Now playing for Getafe, Carvajal also discussed the possibility of returning to Madrid in a coaching role. Carvajal left Real Madrid after making 451 appearances and winning 27 trophies, having progressed through the academy to become a key first-team figure. His departure marks the end of a remarkable chapter, although he is embracing the challenge of proving himself in a different shirt. Dani Carvajal reflects on leaving Real Madrid for Getafe The defender admitted that adapting to his new routine has not been straightforward after so many years travelling to Real Madrid’s training complex at Valdebebas. “I had an incredible send-off – one of the best experiences of my life. “Going out onto the street and feeling the warmth of the Madrid fans, thanking me for everything I’ve done and asking me to come back in the future, is what fulfils me the most – more than the trophies. “Feeling that the fans are proud of how I’ve given my all is the best thing ever. Now at Getafe, I’m treating it as a challenge, and I’m really looking forward to playing.” After a career filled with silverware, Carvajal placed particular importance on the connection he built with Madrid fans. Carvajal now plays for Getafe. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Asked about the defining moments of his 13 years in the first team, he recalled the milestones that shaped his career. “The day of my presentation, without a doubt. The day of ‘La Décima’, which marked the start of a 12-year golden era with a very young squad and academy graduates like Nacho, Morata and Joselu himself. “And I’ll also always remember the day of my farewell.” Carvajal praises Valverde after Real Madrid’s El Clasico victory Despite his move to Getafe, Carvajal followed Real Madrid’s 2-1 victory over Barcelona in El Clásico with considerable emotion. He believed the match demonstrated Madrid’s determination and praised both teams for their performances. “I was nervous. I thought it was a cracking match. Both teams put in a great performance, but Madrid in particular never backed down at any point. “Real Madrid made a statement. It looks different, but I watched it wearing a Madrid shirt.” Carvajal also highlighted Valverde’s ability to contribute in different positions, particularly at right-back, where his physical qualities allow him to influence both phases of play. “He’s very versatile. Thanks to his physical attributes, he flies up and down the pitch; he’s a powerful passer and covers a lot of ground. He’s doing very well.” Carvajal

item.title: Josh Allen climbs NFL MVP rankings without even playing a game
item.description: Josh Allen didn't play a game last week. His NFL MVP stock still went up. The Buffalo Bills quarterback jumped two spots to No. 1 in NFL.com's latest MVP rankings , overtaking San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy despite Buffalo having a bye in Week 7. Allen moved from third to first in the rankings released Tuesday by NFL.com senior writer Kevin Patra. Purdy dropped to second after San Francisco suffered its first loss of the season, a 29-20 defeat against the Atlanta Falcons. Allen has been one of the NFL's most productive players through six games, accounting for a league-leading 17 touchdowns while guiding Buffalo to a 5-1 record. He has completed 66.7% of his passes for 1,504 yards, nine touchdowns and four interceptions while adding 240 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. Some of Allen's most impressive numbers go beyond traditional statistics. Why Josh Allen is No. 1 in NFL MVP rankings Allen leads NFL quarterbacks in several advanced metrics, according to NFL.com's analysis. His 0.29 expected points added per dropback ranks first among quarterbacks, as does his average of 8.8 yards per pass attempt. Allen also ranks second with a 51.7% success rate, a metric that measures how often a quarterback's plays improve his team's expected scoring outlook. Perhaps the most striking statistic is Allen's impact on winning. Allen has accumulated a 229.1% win probability added, more than 111 percentage points ahead of the next-closest quarterback. The metric measures how much individual plays increase or decrease a team's chances of winning based on the game situation. Buffalo leads the NFL in scoring at 32.8 points per game, helping overcome a defense that has allowed 28.5 points per game, which is 30th in the NFL. NFL MVP rankings entering Week 8 Here's NFL.com's top five entering Week 8: Josh Allen, Buffalo Bills: Up two spots Brock Purdy, San Francisco 49ers: Down one spot Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Seattle Seahawks: Previously unranked Kenneth Walker III, Kansas City Chiefs: Down two spots Trevor Lawrence, Jacksonville Jaguars: Down one spot Purdy led the rankings entering Week 7 after guiding San Francisco to six straight victories to start the season. But he struggled in Sunday's loss to Atlanta, completing 27 of 40 passes for 288 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Smith-Njigba moved into third after catching nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown against Kansas City. NFL.com listed Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff and Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams as players who could soon enter the top five. Allen, who won his first NFL MVP award for the 2024 season, is seeking to become the 12th player in league history to win the award multiple times. This article originally appeared on Rochester Democrat and Chronicle: Josh Allen climbs NFL MVP rankings without even playing a game

item.title: Game 4 World Series hero Ben Williamson shares immediate reaction to Rays’ wild win
item.description: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Game 4 World Series hero Ben Williamson shares immediate reaction to Rays’ wild win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tampa Bay Rays pulled off a stunning comeback against the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the World Series at Tropicana Field on Tuesday. The Rays beat the Brewers, 4-3 , in 12 innings to stave off elimination in the best-of-seven series. Ben Williamson was the hero for Tampa Bay, hitting a walk-off single with the bases loaded to drive in Nick Fortes for the wild victory. In the postgame interview, Williamson, who came in as a pinch-hitter, touted the Rays’ resolve and credited his teammates . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Just being ready for the situation. These guys got us in the game, kept us in the game, and to come through, that spot feels good,” said Williamson. “It just shows the resiliency of this group. We continue to fight, and that’s been the motto of this series and this whole season. Just fight.” “We continue to fight and that’s been the motto of this series and this whole season” Ben Williamson talks with @Ken_Rosenthal after he walked it off for the Rays in Game 4 of the 2026 World Series pic.twitter.com/i4QnaP8te1 — FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 28, 2026 The odds are stacked against the Rays , as no team has ever come back from a 3-0 deficit in the World Series. Only the Boston Red Sox have overcome the said hole in a seven-game series in league history. The 25-year-old Williamson delivered Tampa Bay’s first walk-off hit in the playoffs since Brett Philips did it in Game 4 of the World Series in 2020 against the Los Angeles Dodgers. According to MLB.com’s Sarah Langs, it was also the first walk-off win while facing elimination in the Fall Classic since David Freese’s home run for the St. Louis Cardinals in Game 6 of the World Series in 2011 against the Texas Rangers. The Rays will try to stay alive in Game 5 at Tropicana Field on Wednesday. item.title: Tresoldi declared "not for sale" by Club Brugge amid interest from Bayern, Arsenal, Barcelona and other European giants
item.description: Tresoldi declared "not for sale" by Club Brugge amid interest from Bayern, Arsenal, Barcelona and other European giants Club Brugge have ruled out a winter exit for Germany U21 forward Nicolò Tresoldi amid reported interest from several of Europe’s top clubs. The 22-year-old has been linked with Bayern Munich, Arsenal, Barcelona and other European heavyweights after scoring 12 goals in 14 appearances for Brugge this season. However, Belgian newspaper Het Nieuwsblad reports that an unnamed member of the club’s board has declared Tresoldi “not for sale”, ruling out a January move. The situation could change in the summer, though. If Tresoldi continues his impressive form, Brugge may find it difficult to keep hold of the highly sought-after striker. Tresoldi's contract with the Belgian club runs until the summer of 2029.

item.title: Onion price jumps 900% to N300,000 in 6 months
item.description: By Cynthia Alo The price of a 120kg bag of onions jumped from N30,000 in April 2026, to about N300,000 in October representing a 900 percent increase in six months. National Onion Producers, Processors and Marketers Association of Nigeria (NOPPMAN) attributed the increase to inadequate storage facilities and fire outbreaks in warehouses in the North which contributed to post-harvest losses of more than 51 percent within the period. A Vanguard AgroBiz market survey shows that the price of a big sack of fresh onions at Mile 12 Lagos international market is N300,000, while the dried one is between N350,000 to N380,000 as of last week. In an interview with Vanguard AgroBiz, the National President of NOPPMAN, Aliyu Isah, said the price surge was not necessarily due to inadequate national production, but rather the loss of a significant proportion of harvested onions before the next production season. “It’s not that we did not produce enough for the country, but we lost more than 51% from April to October,” he said. Isah attributed the losses to poor storage facilities, fires that destroyed onions in local storage centres and the disruption caused by unsuitable seeds introduced into Nigeria during the 2024–2025 growing season. He said the seed, reportedly brought in from Algeria, was unsuitable for Nigeria’s farming system and caused substantial losses to farmers’ investments. According to him, the seed crisis alone resulted in losses estimated at nearly N100bn, while the sector needed government intervention to prevent the disruption from worsening into a supply shortage. He said government intervention was necessary when a crisis affected an agricultural subsector, warning that failure to address the underlying problems could deepen losses in subsequent seasons. Isah said the Ministry of Agriculture had discussed support for the onion subsector with the Bank of Agriculture and the Nigerian Agricultural Development Fund (NADF), regarding seed supply and farm inputs. He said the association had yet to receive the proposed intervention at the time of the interview, although discussions were ongoing. The support, he added, should help farmers restore production and prevent a repeat of the crisis. Looking ahead, Isah expects supplies from Sokoto to begin around November and December, followed by Aliero in Kebbi State from late December to January. The main harvest season is expected around March and April. He expressed optimism that the incoming harvest would ease prices, but said better storage facilities and timely government support were needed to reduce losses and prevent future shortages. item.title: ❌ Blackout in China: LALIGA matches banned after Mbappé's comments
item.description: ❌ Blackout in China: LALIGA matches banned after Mbappé's comments China's state television has confirmed the indefinite suspension of LaLiga broadcasts in the country, according to the EFE news agency. The drastic measure comes in response to deep anger over remarks made by Kylian Mbappé. China Media Group (CMG) has flatly rejected Real Madrid's explanations. The club argued that the French forward was exercising his freedom of expression without intending to offend, an argument Beijing considers wholly insufficient. The Chinese state broadcaster says the player's remarks “go beyond freedom of expression.” It therefore warns that the Madrid club cannot evade its institutional responsibility for the resulting diplomatic and sporting dispute. The television blackout does not affect only Spanish league matches. The order includes a complete ban on any match or content linked to Mbappé, as well as the immediate withdrawal of his commercial advertising campaigns. China's position on resuming Spanish football broadcasts is firm. item.title: Everton and Crystal Palace put on red alert as Lecce prepare to cash in on breakout Serie A defender Tiago Gabriel in January
item.description: US Lecce v AC Monza - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Premier League sides Everton and Crystal Palace have been handed a major transfer boost ahead of the winter market as Italian outfit Lecce prepare to listen to offers for prized centre-back Tiago Gabriel. Despite tying the 21-year-old defender down until 2030, the Serie A club are willing to sanction his departure in the new year. Italian outfit invite winter bids According to Football Insider , Lecce have decided they are "ready" to cash in on the Portuguese defender and will sell him to the "highest bidder" when the January window opens. Both the Toffees and the Eagles are tracking the youngster closely alongside several leading Italian clubs following his impressive breakthrough campaign last season. Everton boss David Moyes wants to secure his signature despite already boasting strong depth in central defence. Portuguese prospect enjoys rapid rise Although signing a new centre-half is not a pressing winter priority on Merseyside, recruitment chiefs view Gabriel as a talent with a bright future and are ready to pounce as Lecce accept they cannot keep him long-term. As recently as the 2024-25 season, the defender was turning out for Estrela da Amadora's B team in his native Portugal before quickly becoming a cornerstone of the Italian club's senior setup. He missed the starting line-up in just two Serie A fixtures last term as Lecce narrowly avoided relegation to the second tier, and he has already recorded two goals and an assist across six league starts this season. Attacking reinforcements remain urgent priority While Everton weigh up a defensive swoop, former club chief executive Keith Wyness told the same outlet on Tuesday that recruiting a striker in January is far more urgent after missing out on a late summer deal for Folarin Balogun . That failed pursuit has left French forward Thierno Barry as the sole senior centre-forward at Moyes' disposal this season. Although the manager has handled the striker carefully so far, he lacks any alternative options up front, and Wyness believes failing to land another attacker in the summer has already cost the Merseysiders "six points" in the Premier League table. Fierce competition awaits January suitors Securing Gabriel's services in the new year will not be straightforward for Everton given the rival interest from Palace and top Serie A sides. Meanwhile, Moyes must navigate a demanding autumn and festive schedule with a thin attacking department before reinforcements can arrive. How the Toffees balance their winter budget between a much-needed striker and a long-term defensive prospect will define their upcoming transfer window.

item.title: Liverpool face La Liga giants in race for Bundesliga defender
item.description: Liverpool face La Liga giants in race for Bundesliga defender Finn Jeltsch Transfer Race Builds as Liverpool Monitor Stuttgart Centre-Back Liverpool are among the clubs keeping a close eye on Stuttgart defender Finn Jeltsch, with Sport reporting that Barcelona are actively considering the Germany youth international as they assess future options at centre-back. The 20-year-old has emerged as one of the most closely watched young defenders in Europe. Barcelona’s sporting department, led by Deco, are said to value his profile highly, while Liverpool and Real Madrid have also been tracking his development since the early stages of the season. Interest elsewhere is growing too, with Arsenal and Atletico Madrid also mentioned among the clubs aware of his progress. Jeltsch fits the modern mould. He is young, tactically flexible and already operating in a demanding structure at Stuttgart, a side playing Champions League football and asking plenty of their defenders both in and out of possession. For clubs seeking a centre-back capable of defending space behind a high line and contributing with the ball, that combination naturally attracts attention. Finn Jeltsch emerging as elite defensive prospect The report outlines why his stock is rising so quickly. Jeltsch made 37 appearances last season and travelled with Germany for the World Cup, although he did not make his senior debut. Since then, his development has continued at pace. He is now described as a defensive leader at Stuttgart, a notable step for a player still only 20. That rapid growth matters in the current market. Elite clubs are not simply searching for defenders who can head clear and win duels. They want players comfortable receiving under pressure, shifting across the line, holding their position intelligently and recovering in open space. Jeltsch appears to tick a number of those boxes. Barcelona’s interest is framed around that tactical suitability. Hansi Flick is understood to appreciate Jeltsch’s ability to operate in a pressing team with an advanced defensive line, qualities that suit the Bundesliga environment and would, in theory, translate well to his ideas. The same logic explains Liverpool’s attention. Under Andoni Iraola, Liverpool’s defensive planning will be built around mobility, aggression and players who can defend large spaces. Jeltsch’s profile makes sense in that context. He is the sort of signing top clubs explore before a player reaches the very top bracket of the market. Liverpool transfer interest and Araujo question One particularly intriguing detail in the report centres on Liverpool’s existing defensive picture. Sport suggests Barcelona are curious about the overlap between Jeltsch’s position and that of Ronald Araujo, who they say is on loan at Liverpool. The suggestion is that Barcelona could end up linking the Uruguayan’s future, including a reported €55 million clause, to any move involving Jeltsch. item.title: Liverpool star is on par with Van Dijk based on current level
item.description: Liverpool star is on par with Van Dijk based on current level Jeremy Jacquet proving Liverpool right as £55m centre-back settles in alongside Virgil van Dijk Liverpool moved decisively for Jeremy Jacquet in January, and a few months into his Anfield career the early evidence suggests they identified a defender ready for the step up sooner than many expected. According to Sporting Life , the 21-year-old has made an immediate impact since arriving from Rennes, with his performances already helping to reshape the conversation around a transfer that initially drew scrutiny. That scrutiny was understandable at the time. Liverpool committed an initial £55 million for a player who had only a limited body of senior football behind him in France. Chelsea had been working hard on the deal and appeared well placed, with personal terms reportedly advanced, before Liverpool stepped in, met Rennes’ demands and agreed a structure that allowed Jacquet to remain in Ligue 1 for the rest of the campaign. It was a move framed in some quarters as aggressive, expensive and potentially risky. Liverpool had already shown a willingness to spend on proven elite talent, with Florian Wirtz, Hugo Ekitike and Alexander Isak all arriving with strong track records. Jacquet, by contrast, came with far less first-team exposure, which made the fee a natural talking point around the Premier League. Jacquet transfer fee fading into background That is often the clearest sign a signing is working. When a young defender joins for £55 million, every touch can be examined through the lens of cost. When the fee stops dominating the discussion, it usually means the player has settled quickly and begun to justify the club’s conviction. That appears to be where Jacquet is heading already. Liverpool’s defensive numbers have improved markedly. They have kept clean sheets in half of their matches to this point, and Sporting Life notes they rank among the division’s strongest sides for expected goals against. For a team that managed only 10 clean sheets across the whole of last season, that shift is significant. Clean sheets are rarely the work of one player alone, but centre-backs remain central to any improvement in control, spacing and recovery. Jacquet’s individual data adds weight to the visual impression. He has brought pace, composure and authority. A top speed close to 35km/h points to recovery power over distance, while a league pass completion close to 89% suggests a defender comfortable taking responsibility in possession. The volume of line-breaking passes and long distribution also indicates Liverpool are trusting him to start attacks, not merely finish them. Defensively, the profile is equally encouraging. Winning 70% of ground duels and 74% of aerial contests is strong output for any centre-back, let alone one adapting to a new league, new tactical demands and a new defensive partner. item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro on way to Ecuador from Argentina after fleeing Brazil
item.description: Defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro was on his way to Ecuador after fleeing Brazil, Argentina’s government said on Wednesday. Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil’s runoff election to Lula on Sunday, entered Argentina on Tuesday night before boarding a flight to Ecuador, the country’s National Directorate of Migration said on X. The 45-year-old entered Argentina “with valid travel documents and no legal impediment,” it added, despite a court order banning his exit. Bolsonaro, his wife and two daughters boarded “a private flight operated by the company Baires Fly S.A. bound for the city of Guayaquil, Ecuador,” the government agency said. According to data from the Flightradar24 website, the flight took off just after midnight (0300 GMT) on Wednesday from the Argentine town of Puerto Iguazu in the country’s northeast. Baires Fly did not immediately respond to AFP’s request for comment. US media citing anonymous sources had earlier reported that Bolsonaro had arrived in the United States on Tuesday. The US State Department said it would issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family but did not confirm their travel plans. Brazil’s Supreme Court banned Bolsonaro from leaving the country and ordered him to hand over his passports. He is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering, and with his election loss is also set to lose parliamentary immunity. Bolsonaro has not acknowledged his electoral defeat, citing the decision to extend polling hours over transport difficulties that prevented some citizens from voting. item.title: It's over, Liverpool star now relying on €80m gamble to save career
item.description: It's over, Liverpool star now relying on €80m gamble to save career One Liverpool star appears to have no way back. He's depending on a €80m gamble to get things back on track. Liverpool have made some big decisions this season as Andoni Iraola looks to build a team out of this group. Of course, most of those decisions came in the transfer window. But we’ve seen plenty of them since the season started, too. Midfield has been a massive one - Trey Nyoni’s role in the squad continues to get stronger and stronger. Ryan Gravenberch no longer seems to have a place as the main holding midfielder, too, while Lewis Koumas is certainly the no.2 striker in the squad (at least until Hugo Ekitike reappears). But maybe one much bigger decision has been made. One that essentially calls time on one player’s Liverpool career. Jeremie Frimpong has no way back Ronald Araujo has been a revelation. We imagine the initial plan with him was to be a centre-back but fortunately, Jeremy Jacquet has been so good that it makes more sense to use him as a first-choice. That’s allowed Araujo to lock down a position at right-back. The Uruguayan isn’t a modern-day full-back in that he’s not exactly creating chances or offering much width, but he’s a rock-solid defensive force there. And that’s allowed for Liverpool to act without an overlapping player for the winger on that side. They’ve essentially got full license to attack in any way they’d like and it’s working. Rio Ngumoha and Bradley Barcola - both wingers who prefer to attack down the line on that side - have had massively positive impacts in both of Liverpool’s last two games. Having a defence-first full-back before them only helps in that. Not only that, but it’s reduced the need for a defensive midfielder. Liverpool have had more security with a defensive full-back. It also means the right-sided centre-back isn’t needed to constantly cover on that side. But this strategy means is bad news for Jeremie Frimpong . The Dutchman is essentially the opposite of Araujo - a pure attacking player who unquestionably has an effect on the winger in front of him. Having him there asks for more cover from the centre-back, too, suddenly making the need for a defensive midfielder paramount. And so it feels right now like Frimpong can only thrive at Liverpool if they do sign that defensive midfielder - and that the signing is an overwhelming success.

item.title: Barcelona refuse to back down! Catalan giants to appeal €602 fine over Julian Alvarez transfer saga
item.description: VfB Stuttgart v Atletico de Madrid - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Barcelona will fight a fine imposed by the Spanish FA following a dispute with Atletico Madrid over Julian Alvarez. Despite the nominal nature of the financial penalty, the Catalan club remains adamant that their conduct during the summer transfer window was entirely within the rules. Barca contest symbolic RFEF sanction Barcelona are prepared to take their legal battle to the next level as they refuse to accept a symbolic fine from the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF). The club has confirmed it will appeal a €602 penalty triggered by a formal complaint from Atletico. The Rojiblancos alleged that Barca executives engaged in prohibited negotiations with Alvarez while he was still under contract at the Metropolitano, a move that sparked significant friction between the two La Liga powerhouses. The RFEF's extraordinary committee recently concluded that Barcelona committed a "minor infraction" under Article 133 of the federation's disciplinary code. This ruling came after FIFA initially declared itself incompetent to handle the specificities of the domestic dispute. Defiant Catalans refuse to admit guilt According to reports from SPORT , despite the tiny financial nature of the fine, the hierarchy at the Spotify Camp Nou is determined to clear the club’s name, maintaining that their conduct throughout the pursuit of Alvarez was entirely above board. The Barcelona legal department believes that accepting any fine would be an admission of guilt. The club continues to argue that they followed standard protocol by submitting a formal proposal to the Madrid-based side. They contend that the lack of a response from Atletico to their official offer should not preclude them from exploring the viability of a transfer, especially when the player had expressed a desire to move to the Catalan capital. Unanswered offers and broken negotiations The friction between the two clubs was exacerbated by the firm stance taken by Atletico's executive leadership. Throughout the summer, the Rojiblancos were determined to prevent their star asset from joining a direct title rival. This led to a complete breakdown in communication, even as Barcelona sought a marquee replacement for the departing Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres. Atletico maintained that no negotiations were ever on the table. Enrique Cerezo, the president of Atletico, was particularly vocal about the situation during the peak of the transfer window. "There has been, and will be, no negotiation regarding the transfer of Julian Álvarez," the club chief stated. Alvarez issues public apology The player himself has been working hard to repair his relationship with the Atletico supporters after a summer of uncertainty. item.title: ‘We have to be able to…’ – JJ Redick’s blunt statement on the one thing the Lakers need after loss
item.description: Photo by Harry How/Getty Images Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick had a blunt assessment of what the team needs to deliver every night to keep winning after their first loss of the 2026-27 NBA season. The Lakers fell to a 136-129 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers at home on October 27, dropping their record to 3-1 while the Blazers improved to an undefeated 3-0 on the season. The loss was marked by the Lakers being a complete mess defensively, a takeaway that head coach JJ Redick shared after the loss. JJ Redick admits the Lakers’ defence is responsible for loss to Blazers Redick spoke to the media after the game, admitting that the Lakers need to be strong enough defensively to win home games when their offence is producing 129 points on their own. “But we got good looks, and I think we have to be able to rely on our defence every night. If we score 129 points at home, we should be able to get enough stops to win.” “And credit to Portland, for sure. I said it before the game; it was going to be a great test for us because they’re a really good basketball team. They showed that tonight.” Despite the Blazers proving this season that they might be a dangerous team, the Lakers cannot be pleased with an outcome where their offensive stars delivered, but the defence completely collapsed. Shooting variance also has to be factored in, as the Blazers shot 18-for-36 from three for a 50% clip that is not sustainable over an 82-game season. Coach Redick also needs to look at the rotations he is using, as he could not find a great balance between the personnel who need to be key in games. Matisse Thybulle ended the game as a -12, while bench big Sandro Mamukelashvili was a +6. One loss does not define a season, but the Lakers already know what their biggest weakness is and have 78 more games to address that as the season goes on. item.title: Barcelona to appeal RFEF fine over Julian Alvarez transfer approach after Atletico Madrid complaint
item.description: Barcelona to appeal RFEF fine over Julian Alvarez transfer approach after Atletico Madrid complaint Barcelona have decided to challenge a €602 fine imposed by the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) following a complaint from Atletico Madrid over their approach for Julian Alvarez during the summer transfer window, according to MARCA . The Catalan club insists they followed the correct procedures when expressing interest in the Argentine striker and are unwilling to accept the sanction despite its relatively small financial value. The dispute stems from Atletico’s accusation that Barcelona contacted Alvarez without first notifying his club. Barcelona reject that version of events, maintaining that they formally communicated their interest to Atletico but received no response. Barcelona fined by RFEF after Atletico Madrid complaint Atletico Madrid lodged their complaint in July, prompting the RFEF to examine whether Barcelona had breached the regulations governing approaches to players under contract with other clubs. The Spanish federation subsequently imposed a €602 penalty under Article 133 of its disciplinary regulations, which addresses failures to comply with regulatory requirements, official instructions and established obligations. Barcelona will challenge the fine imposed by RFEF. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The matter falls under the jurisdiction of the RFEF rather than FIFA, given the domestic nature of the dispute between the two Spanish clubs. Although the sanction is minor in financial terms, Barcelona believe accepting it would effectively mean acknowledging misconduct that they insist never occurred. Barcelona deny wrongdoing in Julian Alvarez transfer negotiations Barcelona’s position is that their pursuit of Alvarez was conducted through legitimate channels. Club officials maintain that Atletico were formally informed of their interest in the forward, with an offer submitted directly to the Madrid-based club. According to MARCA, Barcelona received no response to that proposal, and negotiations never progressed to the point of an agreement over a transfer fee. Barcelona were interested in Julian Alvarez. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The club considers the €602 punishment almost insignificant financially, but its objection concerns the principle behind the decision rather than the amount involved. Barcelona therefore intend to appeal the fine and any additional sanctions connected to the case, seeking to overturn the federation’s findings. Why Barcelona are challenging the RFEF sanction despite small fine Barcelona’s decision to contest such a modest penalty is a reflection of the importance they place on defending their conduct in the transfer market. The central issue is whether the club’s communication with Atletico satisfied the applicable regulations before any approach involving Alvarez. item.title: La Liga president meets Chinese ambassador as Kylian Mbappe controversy continues to escalate
item.description: La Liga president meets Chinese ambassador as Kylian Mbappe controversy continues to escalate Real Madrid’s impressive victory over Barcelona in Sunday’s Clasico has been overshadowed by an unexpected controversy involving Kylian Mbappe. The French superstar’s remarks about a Chinese political figure have triggered a backlash that now extends well beyond his personal sponsorship agreements. La Liga president Javier Tebas has taken another significant step to contain the situation, holding talks with China’s ambassador to Spain. The controversy is now threatening the league’s commercial and broadcasting relationships with the country. Tebas holds talks with Chinese ambassador over Mbappe controversy On Tuesday, Tebas confirmed that he had met Chinese ambassador Yao Jing to discuss the fallout from Mbappe’s comments and explore possible solutions. “Today I held a meeting with the Chinese ambassador to Spain to address the situation caused by Kylian Mbappe’s statements and seek solutions that will allow us to overcome this episode,” Tebas explained. The controversy originated from an interview on The Bridge , during which Mbappe discussed a meme showing his face superimposed on an image of former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. The reaction has been substantial. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV suspended La Liga coverage and removed promotional material featuring Mbappe. Three Chinese companies have also ended their sponsorship relationships with the Frenchman. Tebas emphasised the importance of protecting La Liga ‘s existing partnerships, particularly its agreement with the Chinese Professional Football League, which runs until 2029. Real Madrid face an uncomfortable situation The developments come despite Mbappe issuing a public apology , acknowledging that his comments were ill-judged and expressing regret for the offence caused. The situation is particularly sensitive for Los Blancos because Mbappe is not simply their leading attacker. He is also one of the club’s most recognisable international figures whose commercial appeal transcends markets. However, there is an important distinction between the consequences affecting Mbappe personally and those affecting Madrid. Kylian Mbappe has found himself embroiled in a controversy after El Clasico. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) While several of his sponsorship agreements have ended, it remains unclear whether the controversy could also affect Real Madrid’s commercial partnerships. Tebas has made it clear that an individual controversy should not damage years of cooperation between Spanish football and China. It remains to be seen whether the fallout from this situation can be resolved amicably and things return to normal sooner rather than later.

item.title: Netanyahu bloc leads after half of Israeli votes counted but no majority
item.description: The camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was ahead of his rival’s opposition bloc but still short of a majority on Wednesday after 50 percent of votes were counted in Israel’s pivotal general election. Voters turned out in the highest numbers in decades to give their verdict on Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister who has pushed the country sharply to the right and unleashed a wave of wars in response to Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack. Following the vote, both Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot vowed to form a government despite neither being projected to win a majority. After 51.8 percent of ballots were counted, Netanyahu’s bloc was shown to have 55 of the 120 seats in the parliament. Eisenkot’s opposition bloc had 49 seats and the Arab parties 16. The partial results are likely to change as more votes are counted. Exit polls had shown that Eisenkot, a former military chief and political novice, and his opposition bloc were neck-and-neck with Netanyahu’s hard-right camp, with both winning about 51 seats, well away from the threshold for a majority in parliament. The strongest gains came from Arab Israeli parties whose voters turned out in soaring numbers against Netanyahu, who has relentlessly warned that the minority would dilute the Jewish nationalist direction in which he has taken Israel. The partial results suggest that Eisenkot’s bloc would have enough seats for a majority if there was a coalition agreement with the Arab parties. But Eisenkot said during the campaign he would not govern with Israeli Arab lawmakers, echoing the position of Netanyahu, who has suggested a government relying on Arab votes would lack legitimacy. Arab lawmakers could also give Eisenkot support in parliamentary votes to maintain a minority government without joining a coalition. A lack of clear majority for either camp could mean weeks spent trying to cobble together coalitions, with possible new elections on the horizon if negotiations fail. A stalemate could in the immediate term benefit Netanyahu, who would remain caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed. Full results are expected by Thursday evening or Friday morning. Netanyahu, greeting cheering supporters at a Jerusalem convention centre after 3 am (0100 GMT) on Wednesday morning, called for a “strong government of the right” and said the “Jewish and Zionist majority must unite”. The 77-year-old prime minister, who has governed Israel on and off for nearly two decades, was unusually brief and did not directly claim victory. US President Donald Trump told reporters on Wednesday that his endorsement of Netanyahu had helped the premier “a lot”. – ‘Public voted for change’ – Speaking to supporters in Tel Aviv, 66-year-old Eisenkot issued a veiled warning to Netanyahu, who observers say could use a war to push for a unity government. “Netanyahu, don’t you dare use Israel’s security for your political needs,” Eisenkot said. item.title: Bayern Munich vs Magdeburg – Match preview and team news
item.description: Bayern Munich vs Magdeburg – Match preview and team news Bayern Munich is set to play Magdeburg at their home ground for their DFB Pokal fixture on Wednesday. Bayern will certainly be looking to win the match comfortably after drawing three of their last five matches in all competitions. Bayern Munich vs Magdeburg – Match preview and team news Date: Wednesday, 28th October. Kick-off: 7:45pm BST Venue: Allianz Arena, Munich. Bayern Munich team news Bayern Munich face severe squad depletion ahead of their DFB-Pokal clash, with assistant coach Aaron Danks managing the touchline as head coach Vincent Kompany continues his hospital recovery. Danks must deploy a heavily rotated “survivor’s lineup” to protect key players before Der Klassiker. Newly crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane is fully available after returning to training, though he may be rested. Winger Lubambo Musonda remains completely ruled out as he continues to rehabilitate from a long-term Achilles tendon rupture. Additionally, Moritz-Broni Kwarteng has been left out of the travelling squad, while midfielder Falko Michel remains a major doubt due to ongoing muscular issues. Sander is expected to field a highly competitive, attacking line-up to exploit Bayern’s heavily rotated defensive unit. Form Bayern Munich FC Bayern Munich remains undefeated in 15 matches across all competitions this season. They sit at the summit of the Bundesliga after bouncing back from a run of three draws in four games with a commanding 3-1 victory over SC Freiburg last weekend. item.title: Better than Brian Lara? Dinesh Karthik decodes the science behind Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s massive backlift punch and brute power
item.description: Better than Brian Lara? Dinesh Karthik decodes the science behind Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s massive backlift punch and brute power originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Dinesh Karthik says Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s power comes from hip-shoulder separation and an unusual backlift. The 15-year-old hit 45 off 19 balls in India’s six-wicket win over New Zealand. Karthik also feels the world champions are in a different league, with nobody close. Dinesh Karthik on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi: Explains power-hitting technique, hip-shoulder separation and backlift Dinesh Karthik certainly believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has something special going on with his bat swing, and the former India wicketkeeper has now explained in some detail how a boy of 15 manages to clear the boundary with such ease. The teenager hits boundaries at will, and he scores at strike rates that look almost unreal on paper. On Tuesday, his 19-ball 45 in Wellington was another reminder of what he can do when he is sent out to open the batting. He and Abhishek Sharma put together a stand of 133 runs, which set up a six-wicket win for India in Wellington. Sooryavanshi was dismissed after a rampaging knock, but Abhishek stayed on and made a century, scoring 113 off 38 balls, and he was named Player of the Match. The result gave India an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match T20I series. MORE: India’s batting belief is reaching frightening levels Karthik pointed to a skill that is known in power-hitting as hip-shoulder separation, and he said the teenager has mastered it. In simple terms, Sooryavanshi opens up his hips and pelvis while keeping his upper body and shoulders turned back, so that the muscles around his core are stretched like a loaded spring. He then lets everything go at once, and the bat head swings into the ball at great speed. The energy in that movement travels up through the body in a chain, starting from the ground, passing through the hips and the core, and finally reaching the shoulders and the bat. That is what produces the torque, and it explains why a slim teenager can hit the ball as far as he does. Here is how Karthik described it: "He's got a lot of mechanisms, right, the way he torques, and it's called a shoulder-hip-shoulder separation; they call it in power-hitting. He's probably one of the best at it, how well he's able to coil, then uncoil as he's able to hit it. It's pure power. He hits it as long as anybody who's playing the game." item.title: From rivals to team-mates - Ball links up with Pope
item.description: James Ball (left) won two silvers with Matt Rotherham for Wales while Aaron Pope (right) piloted Neil Fachie to two golds for Scotland [Getty Images] Henry VIII famously had six wives during his time on the throne. While Para-cyclist James Ball has had a more harmonious time with his pilots than the former king had with his spouses, he too is on to his sixth partner, Aaron Pope. Ball will be hoping for a better relationship with this Pope than Henry VIII had with the papacy! Three months ago, Ball and Pope were rivals at the Commonwealth Games, where the latter piloted Neil Fachie to two golds in Glasgow. Ball and Matt Rotherham, meanwhile, settled for silver in the men's tandem B 1,000m time trial and the men's sprint . Now they are team-mates rather than opponents, Pope will aim to help Ball retain the world titles he won with Steffan Lloyd in 2025. "It's not me, I promise," jokes Ball as he announces his latest new partnership. "I'm now with Aaron, so that's been a lot of learning and that's quite important because it's like a proper reset. "It's like when I had Steff Lloyd for Paris [Paralympics 2024]. It was a whole new exciting time to be on the bike together. We're looking forward to seeing what we can do now." Ball's first taste of world championship glory came with two golds in Los Angeles in 2017 alongside Rotherham, with whom he won the 1km time trial and sprint events. And the Californian city is again on the horizon as it hosts the Paralympics in 2028. For the moment, the focus is the Para-cycling Track World Championships in Apeldoorn, Netherlands, which start on Thursday. "This world championships would be a good place to see where we're at and where the rest of the world is," Ball said. "We've got the big one next year in Paris to sort of solidify our place for LA [Paralympics 2028]." Aaron Pope (right) is the sixth different pilot for James Ball (left) who races as an athlete with a visual impairment [Aaron Pope] While the partnership is in its relative infancy, Ball says there have been some nerves as they ready themselves for action. "I think he [Pope] was quite nervous at the start as well and obviously he wanted to prove that he was good enough sort of thing," Ball said. "But if you're on the programme, you're good enough. Training's been good and it's completely different with every pilot, the way they approach training and how we gel together. "It doesn't take me very long to realise if it's working or not so it's really good to see. I feel like I'm teaching him some things even though he's way better than me power-wise, but it's nice to show some of my experience to him." Ball, 35, has embraced the positivity that can come with change. "Paris [Paralympics 2024] was the crowning moment of what I've achieved and I was like, how can this get any better?" he said. "Changing pilots all the time keeps it fresh though, especially for me. "If we had the same tandem partnership, I feel like you'd find it hard to always progress tho

The Nets traded Kyrie to the Dallas Mavericks that season and have been rebuilding ever since. Why Brooklyn Nets Feared Jaylen Brown Trade Irving using his platform to make controversial stances led to the Nets getting thrown into the media fire. Protests were held outside of Barclays Center when Kyrie couldn’t play due to the vaccine mandate and when he was suspended for the controversial links shared. Many NBA pundits blame Irving for the Brooklyn “big three” with Kevin Durant and James Harden failing. item.title: Kylian Mbappe and La Liga issues apology as Real Madrid star sparks China fury and threatens La Liga TV blackout with 'dictator' joke
item.description: Real Madrid C.F. v RB Leipzig - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Kylian Mbappe has issued a formal apology after a controversial joke regarding former Chinese leader Mao Zedong sparked a major diplomatic and commercial backlash. The Real Madrid forward saw lucrative sponsorship deals terminated and La Liga face a total broadcasting blackout in the region following his ill-judged remarks. Commercial backlash over social media meme Real Madrid superstar Mbappe finds himself at the centre of a diplomatic storm after reacting to a viral internet meme. A circulating video showed the forward mocking an edited image of himself transposed onto the face of former Chinese Communist Party leader Mao Zedong. The Frenchman laughed off the picture, referring to the historical figure as "a Chinese dictator". The incident triggered severe commercial repercussions . State broadcaster China Media Group immediately halted all La Liga television coverage and pulled advertising featuring the France captain. The network cited "seriously negative conduct" as the primary reason for the sudden blackout. Furthermore, major Chinese corporations rapidly severed ties with the player. Drinks manufacturer Dongpeng and dairy giant Mengniu both terminated their lucrative sponsorship agreements with immediate effect, condemning the behaviour as an affront to national sentiments. Mbappe and La Liga issue formal apologies In response to the escalating crisis, Mbappe released a comprehensive apology acknowledging the severity of his misstep. "During a recent interview, I reacted to an image of myself. My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," the forward stated on Tuesday. "I apologise to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history. I am sincerely sorry." La Liga president Javier Tebas quickly followed suit, desperate to protect Spanish football's broadcast interests in the region. "From LaLiga, we deeply regret the statements made by Kylian Mbappe that have caused discomfort and offense in China," Tebas said in a statement . "We understand the harm caused and, on behalf of LaLiga I wish to convey our sincere apologies to the Chinese people. For many years, we have built a relationship of respect, trust and co-operation with China, its authorities, its sports institutions, its audiovisual operators, and millions of fans of Spanish football." Tebas firmly distanced the league from the player's remarks, adding: "We cannot allow an individual action to tarnish that relationship or harm the more than 20 clubs in our professional competitions and millions of Chinese fans. We are taking the measures within our reach and working directly with our partners and interlocutors in China to overcome this situation. Our commitment to China, its people, and its institutions is steadfast. A relat

That exchange provided fresh material for fans after Tatum’s latest heroics.
