item.title: “Did not go unnoticed”: Another shocking reason for Michael Carrick sack decision revealed
item.description: “Did not go unnoticed”: Another shocking reason for Michael Carrick sack decision revealed Manchester United supporters took another huge hit to their confidence in the side when they lost 0-3 at home to AFC Bournemouth on Sunday. The situation Fans had expected a reaction after a tough 1-4 loss to 1907 Como in Italy last Wednesday, but the team somehow managed to play even worse. Old Trafford was naturally an unhappy place, and throughout the game there were chants against the ownership, the director of football Jason Wilcox, and about plans to build a new stadium. The biggest drama arrived at the end of the match, though, as the players were walking off. The Stretford End serenaded their Champions League-winning midfielder Michael Carrick as he walked off the pitch, waving to the crowd. As soon as he disappeared down the tunnel, the fans turned on the players, booing them relentlessly to leave them in no doubt where their anger and blame lay for the shambolic performance. Nonetheless, most felt that Carrick’s run in the job would be coming to an end, but surprisingly it was reported yesterday that the English manager has survived at least a little time longer in the job. In fact, Carrick took training yesterday at 11am as he prepared for the weekend trip to Stamford Bridge. Sources have told ESPN that the fan support on Sunday may have had something to do with the ownership’s decision to keep Carrick for the meantime. The sources claimed, “it did not go unnoticed by the United front office that Carrick received significant support from United fans during and after the defeat to Bournemouth — with most of the frustration directed at the players.” Things do not get any easier for United after their match against Chelsea this weekend. They will then face AS Roma and Aston Villa at home before the November international break. Featured image by Dan Istitene via Getty Images

item.title: ‘Mid-2010s LeBron (James),’ ‘Saved the Steph (Curry) Era’ – Bill Simmons Drops Bold Yaxel Lendeborg Take After ‘Unbelievable’ Performance vs. Denver
item.description: Collage featuring BASKETBALL-NBA/, BASKETBALL-NBA/, and BASKETBALL-NBA-GSW-POR/. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has continued to impress in each of his first four games, and the climb peaked Monday night. The No. 11 overall pick exploded for a game-high 31 points, 12 rebounds, and 6 assists in a 134-114 rout of the Denver Nuggets to help the Warriors to their first win of the season after an 0-3 start. Bill Simmons took notice of Lendeborg’s start and shared his first overreaction of the season’s opening week, reaching for a LeBron James comparison to make his case. Bill Simmons Weighs In on Yaxel Lendeborg With Bold LeBron James ‘Overreaction’ Simmons began with where he stood on the Warriors before Monday’s win, then turned to the rookie: “I was convinced before last night that this was one of the five worst teams in the league and maybe one of the three worst… That leads me to my 1st overreaction after one week. Overreaction #1, Yaxel might have single-handedly saved the Steph era, like for real, and I can’t tell you how good he was in this Denver game last night.” Simmons then built his case for the rookie around a comparison to the league’s all-time leading scorer. “Yaxel looked like mid-2010s LeBron in this game. I don’t say that lightly because mid-2010s LeBron was awesome. They were running the offense through him. He was all over the place on defense. He was rebounding. He was initiating stuff. He was getting to the basket whenever. It was unbelievable.” RELATED: ‘This Kid Is Going to Be Great,’ ‘Warriors Got a Special One’ — Fans React As Yaxel Lendeborg Asks Trio of NBA Legends for Advice Against Nikola Jokić and crew, Lendeborg shot 9-of-19 from the field and 12-of-13 at the free-throw line while adding 4 offensive rebounds and a block to finish plus-27 in 31 minutes. After Monday’s win, Warriors coach Steve Kerr balanced his praise with a reminder of how much the rookie is still learning. “There’s still probably 10 plays that I can pull up on tape, either mistakes defensively or offensively not recognizing something that he needs to recognize,” Kerr said. “Despite all that, he just dominated the game and took over. At 24, in his fourth game. So, pretty impressive.” From playing junior college ball at Arizona Western to getting into a chippy back-and-forth with Luka Dončić, Lendeborg has taken a long road to Monday’s breakout. The rookie has started all four regular-season games and is averaging 21.8 points, 9.3 rebounds, and 4.8 assists, with double-doubles against Memphis and Denver. After the win, Lendeborg was candid about the expectations he had for himself, especially about the work left on the defensive end. “I still have to figure out my weakside help. I gave up a lot of buckets down low. Just thinking my teammates gonna get back, and they’re thinking I’m gonna stay there. So it’s just a little confusing.” READ MORE: ‘This Is Not a Rookie,’ ‘The Warriors Have Done It Again’ — NBA

item.title: Five epic cup shocks after Arsenal’s League Cup humiliation
item.description: Arsenal suffered a stunning League Cup fourth-round defeat at fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday. The Premier League champions lost 5-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in one of the greatest shocks in the history of English football. AFP Sport looks at five other epic cup upsets: Wrexham 2 Arsenal 1 (1992 FA Cup) The previous season 90 places had separated the two clubs in the English Football League, with Arsenal having claimed their second title in three seasons under manager George Graham. Alan Smith put the Gunners in front, but Mickey Thomas’s free-kick levelled matters with 10 minutes remaining and Steve Watkin astonishingly claimed a late winner. Chelsea 2 Bradford 4 (2015 FA Cup) Chelsea won the FA Cup five times between 2006 and 2018, but Jose Mourinho’s Blues were humbled by third tier Bradford at Stamford Bridge. The Premier League leaders went 2-0 up through Gary Cahill and Ramires. But Bradford stormed back and goals from Jon Stead, Filipe Morais, Andy Halliday and Mark Yeates left Chelsea in tatters. Hereford 2 Newcastle 1 (1972 FA Cup) The fourth-round tie that had everything: pitch invasions by Parka-clad fans and Ronnie Radford scoring one of the FA Cup’s greatest FA Cup goals. Malcolm Macdonald put Newcastle ahead eight minutes from time and it seemed as if there would be no fairytale for the non-league outfit. But Radford equalised with a screamer from 25 yards and Ricky George won it for Hereford in extra-time. Liverpool 0 Wimbledon 1 (1988 FA Cup) Wimbledon’s ‘Crazy Gang’ were given no chance to stop Liverpool from claiming a league and cup double in the final at Wembley. Wimbledon had been a third-tier side four years earlier and Liverpool had won the title by a margin of nine points. But Lawrie Sanchez headed home from Dennis Wise’s free-kick before Wimbledon keeper Dave Beasant saved John Aldridge’s penalty to seal the upset. Grimsby 2 Manchester United 2, Grimsby won 12-11 on penalties (2025 League Cup) United trailed 2-0 as Grimsby duo Charles Vernam and Tyrell Warren scored to expose the flaws in their supposedly superior opponents. Bryan Mbeumo and Harry Maguire managed to take the second-round tie into extra-time. But Grimsby won on penalties to leave then-United boss Ruben Amorim shell-shocked. AFP The post Five epic cup shocks after Arsenal’s League Cup humiliation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: Conor Haughey (left) celebrates with Rafaele Cirino after scoring Fleetwood Town’s winning penalty in their unlikely League Cup triumph over Arsenal - PA/Nick Potts Leaving Highbury was a wrench for Arsenal in 2006, but it was not the case 20 years later. They could not wait to get out of the stadium with the same name after a night that left Mikel Arteta looking haunted. Fleetwood Town did not have any marble halls; they did not even have enough space in their car park for the three coaches carrying Arsenal’s entourage, but they have a proud tradition, spirit and, as a result, they will dine out on a result that will be celebrated for months and talked about for decades. Eighty-four rungs separated these teams at kick-off, but, now and again, you get a situation when the floodlights are on, belief is high and the sense of history is prevalent. It is an intoxicating combination and, gloriously, the stars aligned. Mission impossible was completed. Having chiselled out a 1-1 draw in 90 minutes in which Max Dowman was sent off , Fleetwood dispatched five nerveless spot-kicks, the last one thundered in by Conor Haughey after Bruno Guimarães’ penalty was saved by Jay Lynch. “You have got to have confidence, haven’t you?” Haughey asked. “I just thought, I’m going to run up and smack it. It’s incredible. I come from Belfast and if you don’t have confidence, you will get eaten up.” Fleetwood Town players bound forward after watching Haughey’s decisive spot-kick hit the back of the net (above) to stun the champions of England (below) - Getty Images/Lewis Storey Getty Images/Stuart MacFarlane This was ignominious for Arsenal, an elimination from this tournament to rival the 1969 loss in the final to Swindon Town or the 2012 exit to Bradford, then also of League Two. What made this so astonishing was the fact that Mikel Arteta went so strong. You should never be surprised by anything these days, but, even still, an eight-minute delay because of a drone flying over this wonderful little venue would not have been on anyone’s bingo card. Only 57 seconds had been played when Michael Salisbury, the referee, saw a light in the sky and said “stop”. A drone stops play at the Highbury Stadium. https://t.co/TvjNjjACFM — Sky Sports Football (@SkyFootball) October 27, 2026 The precaution was understandable. Only 10 days ago, one idiot escaped from a village to kick a rugby ball off the roof of an apartment block into the Gtech Community Stadium while Brentford and Liverpool were playing and could have caused serious injury. So while the locals harrumphed as the players tried to keep themselves warm, no risk could be taken. Eventually, police apprehended the operator in a nearby park. It was something unfathomable, which was also true of what happened when the contest resumed. The anticipation was that Arsenal would saunter clear against opponents who had lost at Exeter City on Saturday, leaving them 18th in England’s fourth tier, but it only took a few skirmishes to ap

item.title: Mitchell Starc equals Dale Steyn, leaves several legends behind in elite list
item.description: Mitchell Starc produced a devastating spell to claim his 20th five-wicket haul in Test cricket, helping Australia stage a remarkable comeback against South Africa on the opening day of the deciding third Test at Newlands on Tuesday. The left-arm pacer returned figures of 6/72 as South Africa collapsed from 203/1 to 329 all out after appearing firmly in control of the contest. His latest haul also took his tally of five-wicket hauls in international cricket to 29, placing him alongside Dale Steyn among the most prolific fast bowlers in the format. Starc now has 20 five-wicket hauls in Tests and nine in ODIs. He has moved to the top of the list of active fast bowlers with the most five-wicket hauls in Test cricket, ahead of Kagiso Rabada, who has 17, and Jasprit Bumrah, who has 16. In the all-time list of fast bowlers with the most five-wicket hauls in international cricket, Starc sits sixth, behind Richard Hadlee (41), Glenn McGrath (36), Waqar Younis (35), James Anderson (34) and Wasim Akram (31). South Africa had looked set for a commanding first-innings total after openers Aiden Markram and Marques Ackerman added 140 runs. Ackerman made 95 off 94 balls, while Markram scored 78 as the hosts reached 203/1. However, Starc triggered a dramatic collapse, removing David Bedingham for 50 and Wiaan Mulder for a duck in quick succession. After South Africa recovered through a 95-run seventh-wicket partnership between Marco Jansen and Ryan Rickelton, Starc returned with the second new ball to dismantle the tail. 135255001 He dismissed Rickelton for 42 before bowling Jansen for 52. Starc then claimed Gerald Coetzee and Kagiso Rabada for consecutive golden ducks, completing a stunning turnaround as South Africa lost four wickets in six balls. His figures of 6/72 were also his best against South Africa in Test cricket, improving on his previous best of 6/154 in Perth in 2012. The series remains level at 1-1, with the third Test set to determine the winner. item.title: Barcelona plot shock move for struggling Tottenham star just weeks after he signed new contract until 2031
item.description: Sydney FC v Tottenham Hotspur: Sydney Super Cup - Getty Images Sport Spanish heavyweights Barcelona have revived their pursuit of Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Lucas Bergvall after the youngster struggled to command regular minutes in north London this season. Despite the 20-year-old Sweden international penning a fresh five-year extension only last month, top clubs across Europe are closely monitoring his situation. Catalan giants revive previous pursuit According to TEAMtalk , the Blaugrana are assessing the Scandinavian playmaker again after watching his game time dip under head coach Roberto De Zerbi. Following the summer arrivals of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, the midfielder has logged just 144 Premier League minutes across two starts and two substitute outings alongside two Carabao Cup appearances. That lack of action has alerted several European suitors despite his new deal running until 2031 . Technical profile suits Camp Nou Barcelona previously tracked the midfielder closely during his spell at Swedish side Djurgarden back in 2024 before losing the race for his signature to Tottenham . The report notes that Camp Nou recruitment chiefs still admire his athleticism, technical ability, and versatility across multiple central roles. Club officials view the youngster as a long-term addition capable of developing into an important player alongside established young midfielders Pedri, Gavi, and Marc Bernal, though breaking into that engine room would present fierce competition. Italian heavyweights consider winter approaches The same outlet reveals that Serie A outfits Napoli and Juventus are also keeping close tabs on developments in the English capital. Napoli have added the Swede to their shortlist as they prepare for potential midfield changes, with sources indicating that moving to southern Italy would offer him a clearer pathway to regular starts than switching to Catalonia. Meanwhile, the publication states that Juventus have shown the strongest immediate interest by targeting a six-month loan in January to ease their midfield injury crisis, although Spurs hold all the cards and currently have no desire to sanction a temporary exit. Upcoming fixtures determine winter plans Whether the admiration from Spain and Italy turns into formal bids will depend on how many minutes Bergvall receives over the coming months. Currently sitting 14th in the Premier League table, De Zerbi's side host Crystal Palace on matchday nine this weekend looking to climb the standings. For now, the north London hierarchy remain reluctant to let their developing prospect leave ahead of the winter transfer window.

item.title: MLB lockout key dates to know: Here are the next steps after 2026 World Series for owners vs. players
item.description: MLB lockout key dates to know: Here are the next steps after 2026 World Series for owners vs. players originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the end of the 2026 MLB season comes more uncertainty than the league has had in a number of years. The expiration of the collective bargaining agreement (CBA) between the owners and players is expected to trigger a lockout, meaning the timeline for baseball is very much up in the air ahead of the 2027 season. With owners pushing for a salary cap and salary floor while players insist they won't budge, the next few months could get messy. The lockout doesn't start the moment the season ends, but the pressure is already on for both sides to start working toward a deal to avoid MLB's most significant work stoppage in decades. Here are the key dates to know for MLB's impending lockout, including when it will begin. MORE: 5 big things to know about impending MLB lockout When does MLB lockout start? MLB is expected to lock out the players upon expiration of the CBA on Dec. 1 at 11:59 p.m. ET. While the expiration of the CBA doesn't automatically trigger a lockout, MLB enacting a lockout is simply a formality. That means, until the night of Dec. 1, the offseason can proceed as normal. Awards will be handed out in November, and free agents are free to sign throughout November. Once the lockout begins, however, all transactions are halted and teams cannot make contact with any player on their 40-man roster. MORE: Ranking the top 16 MLB free agents MLB lockout key dates timeline The only date set in stone pertaining to the lockout is Dec. 1, when the CBA expires and MLB will presumably lock out the players. There is no official deadline to hammer out a new CBA, but the 2021-22 lockout tells us what the league's deadlines might be when it comes to starting the season on time. Here are the dates to keep in mind: Dec. 1, 2026: Lockout begins If there is no new CBA in place, which is the expectation, MLB is set to lock out the players upon the previous CBA's expiration at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. At that point, all transactions would end, teams cannot contact players on the 40-man roster and teams stop using the likeness of their players. The start of the lockout could be preceded by a flurry of free-agent deals and even some trades, as it acts as a deadline to get business done before the indefinite pause. In 2021, Corey Seager, Max Scherzer, Javier Baez and Marcus Semien were members of a loaded free-agent class to sign deals in the days leading up to the lockout, but Freddie Freeman, Kyle Schwarber, Kris Bryant and more waited until after the lockout to sign. February 2027: Negotiations ramp up MLB and the MLPA negotiated over Zoom during the 2021-22 offseason until in-person meetings began and started to become frequent in mid-February. item.title: DFB-Pokal Preview: Schalke & Hoffenheim travel to 2. Bundesliga sides, Regionalliga test for high-flying Hertha, Wagner seeks first Hannover win
item.description: DFB-Pokal Preview: Schalke & Hoffenheim travel to 2. Bundesliga sides, Regionalliga test for high-flying Hertha, Wagner seeks first Hannover win Schalke and Hoffenheim will face 2. Bundesliga teams away from home on Wednesday, while Hertha, Hannover and Kaiserslautern are also all in action. Dynamo Dresden vs. Schalke 04 Miron Muslić’s side have managed to replicate their excellent defensive record in the Bundesliga, but issues in the final third meant they're in the relegation zone despite only FC Bayern and Borussia Dortmund conceded fewer goals than them. Schalke did score five in the first round of the DFB-Pokal against Hallescher, and they will now hope to repeat that feat against 2. Bundesliga strugglers Dynamo Dresden. The atmosphere in this tie would make this a standout fixture because of the huge reputations of their fanbases. Holstein Kiel vs. TSG Hoffenheim Hoffenheim's trip to Kiel will be a game between two clubs who show signs of improvements in their respective last two games. The hosts became the first 2. Bundesliga club to take points off runaway leaders Hertha before recording their first win of the season against Dresden on Sunday. Hoffenheim's season was going in the wrong direction before successive 3-0 wins over the then-Ligue 1 leaders Lyon and high-flying Bayer Leverkusen. Hoffenheim beat Kiel 3-1 in a pre-season friendly back in July. Hannover 96 vs. 1. FC Kaiserslautern In the only tie involving two 2. Bundesliga clubs, Sandro Wagner's Hannover will host the in-form Kaiserslautern side. The visitors are level on points with second-placed Nürnberg after they beat Miroslav Klose's side on matchday 9. On the contrary, pre-season promotion favorites Hannover are in the relegation zone as Wagner has only picked up a single point from three games after replacing Christian Titz. Kaiserslautern's last win in Hannover came in January 2023. SSV Jeddeloh vs. Hertha BSC Regionalliga side Jeddeloh eye to knock out a second 2. Bundesliga side after beating Heidenheim 5-2 in the first round. However, they have only picked up 11 points in 11 league games since their surprising win a couple of months ago. Hertha extended their 2. Bundesliga lead to seven points after their late win over Arminia Bielefeld on Friday. However, Stefan Leitl's men needed a penalty shootout to get past 3. Liga outfit Saarbrücken in the first round of the DFB-Pokal.

item.title: ‘A very sad day’: Arteta despair as Arsenal stunned by Fleetwood
item.description: Mikel Arteta said Arsenal’s stunning League Cup defeat by fourth-tier Fleetwood was “a very sad day” as the Premier League champions suffered one of the most embarrassing results in their history. Arteta’s side crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible fourth round upset after the tie finished 1-1 in normal time. Arsenal’s Bruno Guimaraes had his penalty saved by Jay Lynch in the shoot-out and Conor Haughey scored Fleetwood’s winner. Aaron Loupalo-Bi’s first-half goal had put Fleetwood ahead before Viktor Gyokeres equalised after the interval. Arsenal’s 16-year-old rising star Max Dowman was sent off for violent conduct in the closing stages. Arteta paid the price for prioritising Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool as his decision to make nine changes backfired spectacularly. The Gunners boss conceded Arsenal could have no complaints, admitting it was a painful moment in his reign. “First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through the next round. The manner that they have done it, and for us a very sad day,” Arteta said. “There is nothing to criticise the players for their attitude, their application. “The determination, you could see that was there from the start, even with 10 men. But we conceded a really poor goal to start with that gave them some momentum. “Obviously we have so much of the ball, so many chances, so many shots, and if you want the margins to be bigger than going to the penalties, you need to capitalise on that. And we didn’t. “It’s football, that’s the beauty of this competition. It’s a very sad day.” Arsenal had moved level on points with Premier League leaders Manchester City after a 2-0 victory over Everton on Saturday. But instead of extending their run of 11 wins from their 13 previous games, Arteta’s team returned to north London red-faced after a loss that ranks among the darkest days in the club’s glittering history. “Zero problem attitude-wise. Otherwise, I would be here absolutely fuming. I’m sad, I think we are all sad. We have a massive responsibility to carry this badge in the best possible way,” Arteta said. “You don’t capitalise, then you cannot go through to the next round. Unfortunately, we are out.” – ‘I just can’t believe it’ – Although it looked a harsh decision to send off Dowman for aiming a kick towards Harrison Neal, Arteta was unimpressed with the 16-year-old, giving him a stern word as the midfielder trudged off. “Something that we discussed already before the match,” Arteta said when asked what he told Dowman. “It’s difficult to see on the cameras like that, so I prefer to watch it back properly and then I can assess the situation.” Fleetwood made a mockery of the 84 places between the clubs in the English football system with a defiant display that stopped Arsenal establishing any momentum. Their refusal to be overawed by Arsenal’s star-power was a tribute to Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor, who won the tactical battle with Arteta by sitting deep and attacking on the counter. “I ju

item.title: Nigerian extradited from Benin to US over alleged $100m tax fraud
item.description: A 43-year-old Nigerian, Akinade Adedeji Raheem, has been extradited from Benin to the United States to face federal charges over an alleged scheme involving more than $100 million in fraudulent tax refund claims using stolen identities. Raheem was arraigned in a US federal court following his extradition and ordered detained in the custody of the US Marshals Service pending further proceedings, according to the US Department of Justice. Prosecutors alleged that Raheem and his co-conspirators filed more than 300 fraudulent tax returns between 2018 and 2023, seeking over $100 million in refunds from the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). US Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg said the alleged operation involved hundreds of stolen identities and significant financial losses. “Raheem and his co-conspirators allegedly obtained hundreds of stolen identities, filed fraudulent tax returns using that information, and laundered the proceeds through prepaid debit cards and purchases of used cars that were shipped to Nigeria and other locations,” Hertzberg said. “The scope of the alleged fraud is staggering. Thanks to the dedication of the prosecution team and our law enforcement partners around the world, Raheem has been extradited to the United States,” he added. The indictment also named Abayomi Quadri Eletu, a resident of the United Kingdom and Nigeria, as an alleged co-conspirator. Eletu was indicted separately and arrested in the UK, where extradition proceedings are pending. According to court documents, the suspects allegedly obtained the personal information of American taxpayers and tax professionals, including names, addresses and Social Security numbers, to facilitate fraudulent claims. Investigators said the alleged scheme involved creating online IRS accounts to access private taxpayer information, filing false returns and directing refunds to prepaid debit cards linked to addresses controlled by the suspects. Prosecutors further alleged that Raheem, Eletu and others laundered some of the proceeds by purchasing money orders in amounts intended to avoid reporting requirements. The money was allegedly used to acquire used cars through auction platforms, some of which were shipped to Nigeria, as well as designer clothing and other items. Special Agent in Charge Christopher J. Altemus Jr. of the IRS Criminal Investigation Texas Field Office said the alleged scheme affected hundreds of taxpayers. “Raheem is an alleged co-conspirator in a nationwide identity theft scheme that victimised hundreds of taxpayers. The fraud also stole from the US Treasury, impacting programmes serving us all,” Altemus said. He added that authorities were working internationally to bring suspects in financial crimes to justice. “We are pursuing financial criminals to take back the stolen money and their freedom,” he said. item.title: French Senate passes bill to make protesters pay for unrest damage
item.description: The French parliament’s upper house passed a bill Wednesday that would make protesters financially liable for damage caused during street demonstrations, despite warnings from critics that it could curb the right to protest. The bill was drafted in response to riots that followed Paris Saint-Germain’s victory over Arsenal in the UEFA Champions League final in May. But it has taken on added significance after weeks of protests over inequality and soaring prices culminated in some of the worst violence France has seen in years on October 17, when thousands of businesses across the country were damaged and looted. The Senate passed an expanded version of the bill by 229 votes to 105, backed by a right-wing and centrist alliance which holds a majority. The legislation has been sent to the National Assembly, which is split between France’s political factions, for debate and voting. Far-right leader Marine Le Pen, whom opinion polls place as the frontrunner to succeed Emmanuel Macron in next spring’s presidential election, supports the legislation. Speaking in parliament, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez stressed the “urgency” of responding to the damage and scenes of chaos seen on October 17. “We can no longer allow the vast majority of our fellow citizens to pay for a minority of vandals,” he said. – ‘Legal travesty’ – Under the legislation, protesters could be ordered to pay up to 10,000 euros for damage caused during street demonstrations. But critics argue that people who took no part in vandalism could nonetheless be held liable if they were deemed to have been associated with those responsible. The bill introduces joint financial liability for anyone found to have “knowingly participated” in a group formed with the intent of carrying out acts of vandalism. It would also apply to individuals who “voluntarily” continued to take part in a gathering likely to disrupt public order after two police dispersal warnings. Welfare benefits and housing assistance could also be seized to help cover the cost of damages under the scheme, a provision that has drawn sharp criticism from left-wing parties and advocacy groups. In the second reading, senators toughened the measure to include other social benefits such as the family supplement, back-to-school allowance and the employment bonus. Left-wing lawmakers accused the government of an “authoritarian drift” at the expense of the freedom to demonstrate. Communist senator Fabien Gay denounced what he called a “legal travesty that deliberately conflates protesters and rioters”. Green senator Melanie Vogel accused the government of responding to social demands with “collective punishment.” Supporters of the bill sought to reassure critics. “We must not give the impression that this bill would criminalise a passer-by or a peaceful protester,” said Olivier Bitz of the centre-right Horizons party. – ‘Disastrous consequences’ – The government has proposed introducing protest bans targeting the most violent individuals

item.title: The Signal: The Parties Are Choosing Sides. Will the Voters Follow?
item.description: Tinubu’s political alliances are expanding, Obi and Kwankwaso are sharpening their challenge, and INEC is under pressure to demonstrate transparency. But as the presidential campaign gathers momentum, Nigeria’s politicians may be discovering that winning endorsements is easier than winning public confidence. There is an interesting contradiction emerging in Nigerian politics. At a time when political parties are supposed to be competing against one another, their leading figures are increasingly finding reasons to work together. In Rivers State, Nyesom Wike is assembling a coalition that crosses party boundaries but supports President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates. In Osun, Governor Ademola Adeleke supports Tinubu’s re-election while insisting that his political organisation will compete against the APC in legislative elections. Meanwhile, Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso have established a joint presidential campaign structure, even as other opposition leaders continue discussing the possibility of a broader alliance. And the Independent National Electoral Commission, caught in the middle of growing political suspicion, has taken a step towards addressing concerns about the voters’ register. Welcome to Nigeria’s 2027 election. A contest in which party labels are becoming increasingly flexible, political loyalties are being renegotiated, and the electorate is being asked to distinguish between genuine conviction and political convenience. But beneath the manoeuvring lies a question that could determine the outcome. The politicians are choosing sides. Will the voters follow them? Wike’s coalition: when political boundaries become optional Nyesom Wike has never been a politician easily constrained by conventional party loyalties. His support for Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, despite his association with the PDP, demonstrated his willingness to pursue political objectives across party lines. Now, with another presidential election approaching, he is taking that approach further. At a political gathering in Eleme, Rivers State, Wike made it clear that his Rainbow Coalition is not simply an arrangement to support Tinubu’s re-election. It also intends to support APC candidates contesting governorship and legislative elections. That is a significant development. It suggests that Wike is attempting to create a political structure capable of influencing elections at several levels, regardless of the formal party affiliations of those participating. There is a certain political logic to the arrangement. For Tinubu, Wike provides an influential ally in a strategically important state. For Wike, cooperation with the President offers a means of preserving political relevance and strengthening his position in Rivers. But what does the arrangement offer ordinary voters? That is the question that deserves more attention. Cross-party cooperation is not inherently objectionable. Indeed, democracies often require politicians to work across partisan

item.title: Trump says Putin-Zelensky meeting to be set up ‘very soon’
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that a meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky would be set up “very soon.” The announcement came as Trump’s administration ramps up diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the Russia-Ukraine war, now in its fifth year. “There’ll be a meeting set up very soon and I think a lot of progress could be made,” Trump told reporters. Zelensky said on Sunday that a trilateral meeting between Kyiv, Washington and Moscow would take place in November, aiming to restart stalled peace talks. The Kremlin had previously said that a meeting between the three countries was planned to take place in the United Arab Emirates in November. Putin, who ordered the February 2022 invasion of Ukraine, has consistently rejected face-to-face talks with Zelensky and insisted Moscow intends to seize the rest of eastern Ukraine. Trump came to power in January 2025 promising to end the war in 24 hours — but over a year of US-led talks have failed to produce a breakthrough, with tens of thousands killed. In recent days Trump has once again pivoted away from Ukraine and back to Putin, trumpeting what he said was a deal for Russia to sell diesel and reduce prices sent soaring by his Iran war. item.title: FG moves to secure farms, attract investors
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has moved to address insecurity threatening agricultural investments, signing a partnership agreement to develop security arrangements for farms and attract investors to multibillion-dollar soybean and sugarcane projects in Yobe and Jigawa states. The Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI), Integranium Holdings and Defence Agricultural Assets and Projects Development Company (DAPCO), supported by Defence Holding Company Limited, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Abuja. Speaking at the signing ceremony, Dr Femi Ogunseinde, MOFI’s Executive Director, Investments, said: “We have a soybean initiative in Yobe, we have a sugarcane initiative in Jigawa—all large-scale, all multibillion-dollar projects. “Without having that security anchor to ensure that whatever comes from wherever to invest, the investments are safe, it becomes very difficult for us to do anything.” He said the partnership would provide a platform to approach prospective investors with security arrangements designed to protect their investments. Also speaking, the Managing Director of MOFI, Dr Armstrong Takang, said: “Nigeria needed to make better use of its land, water resources and people to produce sufficient food for households and industries, while generating additional supplies for export.” He said the partnership would focus on developing bankable agribusiness opportunities capable of attracting public and private investment. On his part, DAPCO Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Aliyu Abdulhameed, said: “The defence establishment’s role was to ensure that financing reached agricultural opportunities in rural areas under secure and properly structured arrangements.” He added that surrounding communities would be involved in projects established in their areas, while serving military personnel and veterans would also be considered. Ogunseinde said: “An estimated 30 million to 35 million hectares of land could be available for farming, providing considerable scope for expanding large-scale agricultural production.” He added that the partners had identified several opportunities and expected at least one project to break ground before year-end, although he did not identify the project or specify a commencement date. The Group Managing Director of Defence Holding Company Limited, Air Vice Marshal A.V. Ndache, said: “The memorandum of understanding signed by the institutions was a broad agreement covering agriculture, hospitality and other investment areas.” The post FG moves to secure farms, attract investors appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Cooking gas supply rises 18% to 4.5m litres daily — NMDPRA
item.description: By Ediri Ejoh Domestic supply of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), popularly known as cooking gas, rose by 17.78 per cent year-on-year, YoY, to 4.5 million litres per day in September 2026, from 3.7 million litres per day in September 2025. The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, NMDPRA, disclosed this in its latest data obtained by Vanguard. On a month-on-month, MoM, basis, supply increased by 33.33 per cent from 4.5 million litres per day in August 2026. Meanwhile, the price of cooking gas rose by 7.14 per cent to N1,400 per kg in October 2026, from N1,300 per kg in September. Reacting, former National President of the Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers, NALPGAM, Mr. Oladapo Olatunbosun, attributed the increase to improved local production but called for sustained investment and government support to prevent shortages. He said: “Local production has increased, which is the reason for the result. However, there is much to be done by both the government and stakeholders to drive the development required to harness the potential of LPG.” Olatunbosun urged the government to encourage indigenous operators and support major domestic producers, including Dangote Petroleum Refinery, to boost output and stabilise the energy market. “The government should continue to encourage indigenous operators, and they should see it as being a partner in bringing stability to energy,” he said. He also called for affordable supplies to surrounding communities, adding that increased investment in production and distribution would improve availability. “The market is wide and large, and the more we get people investing in the production and distribution of LPG, the more available the product will be,” he said. Similarly, National President of the Oil and Gas Services Providers Association of Nigeria, OGSPAN, Mazi Colman Obasi, described the supply growth as positive but stressed that consumers must benefit through improved access and affordability. “The growth in supply is a positive development because availability is fundamental to the expansion of LPG consumption. However, the real test is whether consumers are seeing improved access and more affordable prices,” he said. Obasi cautioned that increased supply would not automatically reduce retail prices, citing transportation, logistics, exchange-rate movements and other costs. He said efficient distribution was essential to ensure additional volumes reach consumers and encourage more households to switch to LPG. item.title: 2027: NDC campaign DG urges Atiku to join Obi-Kwankwaso
item.description: The Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Campaign Council, Ibrahim Abdulkarim, has urged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and other opposition leaders to join the alliance backing Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Abdulkarim said the opposition needed to unite behind a common platform to improve its chances of defeating the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the election. Speaking on Arise News, he said the coalition was already taking shape within the NDC, with Obi emerging as its presidential candidate and Kwankwaso agreeing to work with him. “The opposition has to come together for us to win. The opposition have already come together. Nobody said the coalition must happen on ADC. It can happen in NDC, and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso has already dropped his ambition,” he said. Abdulkarim said Atiku and other opposition figures were welcome to join the alliance to broaden its national reach. “What we are asking for is for other people to join us, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, to join all of us, so at least we will have the spread that they think they can add,” he added. The NDC campaign chief also dismissed criticism of the party’s campaign structures, arguing that its organisation should not be compared with the Obidient movement and other support groups backing Obi. “How can you compare a party with a support group? We don’t have any problem. They’re all part of the NDC party. We have more than a thousand support groups like that,” he said. On concerns about electoral fraud, Abdulkarim urged Nigerians who feared their votes might not count to support the NDC, promising that the party had developed measures to protect votes during the 2027 elections. He said the party would campaign peacefully across the country and mobilise voters who had lost confidence in the electoral process. “We are going to do our campaign peacefully. We are going to go into every corner,” he said. Abdulkarim added that the party would reassure voters before the election that their votes would be protected. “I can promise anybody, anybody that feels he wants his vote to count, we have a very, very unique and serious programme that we have put in place,” he said. The post 2027: NDC campaign DG urges Atiku to join Obi-Kwankwaso appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ebonyi Assembly unanimously backs state police bill
item.description: The Ebonyi House of Assembly on Tuesday unanimously approved a bill seeking to establish state police services, endorsing a constitutional amendment transmitted by the National Assembly. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that all 24 members voted in favour of the bill after extensive deliberations and consultations with their constituents. The proposed amendment seeks to alter the 1999 Constitution, as amended, to provide a legal framework for state police services while retaining the Nigeria Police Force at federal level. The Speaker, Moses Odunwa, said the unanimous decision demonstrated the assembly’s commitment to constitutional reforms aimed at strengthening the state’s security architecture. “This will also enhance access to criminal intelligence and protection of lives and properties,” Odunwa said. He described the demand for sub-national policing as a longstanding aspiration among Ebonyi residents. “The demand for a sub-national policing system has been an age-long clamour among Ebonyi people,” he said. Odunwa added that the state had formally presented its position in support of state police during a public hearing organised by the National Assembly on constitutional review. He said the bill’s passage reflected residents’ desire for a policing system closer to communities and more responsive to local security challenges. The Leader of the House, Kingsley Ikoro, said establishing state police would significantly increase manpower in the state’s security sector. Ikoro, who represents Afikpo North West under the All Progressives Congress (APC), said the proposed system would improve efforts to tackle crime at grassroots level. Other lawmakers, including Victor Nwoke (APC–Abakaliki North) and Oluchukwu Ezeali (APC–Afikpo North East), also stressed the importance of bringing policing closer to communities. They argued that decentralised policing could help address Nigeria’s security challenges by improving local responses to crime and criminal activities. Following the bill’s passage, Odunwa directed the Clerk of the House, Mrs Uche Edene, to formally transmit the assembly’s resolutions to the National Assembly. item.title: Why 5G remains out of reach for most Nigerians
item.description: …High cost of devices, coverage remains uneven …As smartphone market contracts 11% amid rising device prices …Africa’s budget smartphone shipments plunge 34% amid rising costs By Juliet Umeh Nigeria’s mobile market has shifted significantly towards newer network technologies over the past three years, but 5G remains out of reach for most consumers. High smartphone prices, uneven network coverage and rising infrastructure costs continue to limit adoption, despite growing demand for mobile data. In May 2023, 2G accounted for 58.36 percent of reported mobile connections, while 4G represented 25.06 percent and 5G just 0.12 percent. By August 2026, 4G had become the leading technology at 54.77 percent, while 2G fell to 36.05 percent. 5G increased to 4.92 percent. The data from the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, show progress but underline how slowly the newest technology is reaching the wider population. Chief Technology Officer of NATCOM Development and Investment Limited, trading as NTEL, Kingsley Uwazie, said Nigerians had a strong appetite for data consumption, but the cost of accessing 5G remained a significant barrier. “The 5G ecosystem is in its maturity phase. It has been proven that there is an appetite. Nigerians have an appetite to consume data. But there is a barrier to acquiring the devices and using the technology,” he said. High cost of compatible devices Consumers need 5G-enabled smartphones to access the technology, but rising device prices are making upgrades increasingly difficult, particularly for low-income earners. Uwazie said 5G devices remained expensive despite subsidies offered by some operators. “5G, at the moment, is not a cheap technology to deploy or to own. The cost of 5G devices has been high,” he said. He cited MTN Nigeria and Airtel Nigeria as operators subsidising selected devices, adding that a phone available for about N50, 000 with a subsidy could cost more than N200, 000 without it. The affordability challenge has intensified as Nigeria’s smartphone market contracted by 11 percent in the second quarter of 2026, according to technology research firm Omdia. Rising memory-chip costs, partly linked to growing demand from artificial intelligence, AI, data centres, have increased pressure on manufacturers and consumers. Across Africa, shipments of smartphones priced below $100 fell by 34 percent year-on-year during the quarter. In Nigeria, a market assessment published by technology news platform Condia found that prices of selected Tecno, Infinix, Oppo and itel models increased between January and June 2026. The midpoint price of the itel S-Series Ultra rose from about N263, 500 to N316,400, while the Infinix Zero Series increased from approximately N550,000 to N637,500. Omdia warned in June that Nigerian smartphone prices could rise by another 15 to 30 percent through the remainder of 2026 if component costs continued increasing. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 28, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian Naira maintained relative stability against the United States Dollar across both official and parallel foreign exchange markets on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Continued liquidity injections by the Central Bank of Nigeria and sustained foreign currency inflows from autonomous channels have helped cushion the local currency against aggressive market pressures. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, the Naira traded around 1,341.31 to 1,352.87 per Dollar. Spot market activity recorded moderate intra-day fluctuations as commercial banks and institutional buyers satisfied forex demand for import bills and capital remittances. The tight corridor underscores ongoing market clearing measures established under the refined operational framework of the central bank. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, Bureau De Change operators and street currency traders in major hubs such as Lagos, Abuja, and Kano quoted buying rates near 1,375 Naira per Dollar and selling rates around 1,390 Naira per Dollar. This keeps the premium between the official window and the unauthorised market relatively narrow. Financial analysts attribute the steadying market conditions to disciplined monetary policy, steady national foreign exchange reserves hovering around key operational benchmarks, and balanced seasonal demand. Market participants expect trading volumes to remain steady over the near term as both official and informal windows absorb regular commercial order flows. item.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 5043-5049: Preparing to Drill at ‘Nazca’
item.description: Curiosity Navigation Curiosity Home Mission Overview Where is Curiosity? Mission Updates Science Overview Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Curiosity Raw Images Images Videos Audio Mosaics More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home 4 min read Curiosity Blog, Sols 5043-5049: Preparing to Drill at ‘Nazca’ NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity acquired this close-up image using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI), showing the abundance of roughly disc-shaped potential crystal forms on our next drill target, informally named “Nazca.” The scratches made by the DRT brush are also visible in this image. MAHLI, located on the turret at the end of the rover’s robotic arm, uses an onboard focusing process to make a composite of images of the same target acquired at different focus positions, to bring multiple features into focus in a single image. Curiosity composed the image on Oct. 18, 2026, Sol 5048 (Martian day 5,048 of the Mars Science Laboratory Mission), at 12:19:51 UTC. NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS Written by Lucy Lim, Planetary Scientist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center Earth planning date: Friday, Oct. 16, 2026 Following the Basque Lakes drill campaign , Curiosity has returned to a spot just a few meters away from the “Chiu Chiu” block to conduct our next drill campaign. “Chiu Chiu” itself wasn’t a good candidate for drilling but the block just beyond it was much more promising, so it became our drive target during Monday’s planning. I was on planning Friday as Geology and Mineralogy Science Theme Lead when we received our close-up views of the neighbor block from the post-drive imaging and our team was happy to see that it was jam-packed with the “disc- and needle-” shaped lumps, just like “Chiu Chiu.” We quickly gave the science go-ahead to proceed with preparations for drilling at the newly named “Nazca” site. One major hypothesis about how the “discs and needles” texture formed is that the characteristic shapes were originally created during the growth of crystals, or “crystal forms.” Minerals will tend to grow into specific shapes depending on their microscopic crystal structure, similar to the salt crystals that you can grow in your kitchen as a home science project. (Maybe you have grown one of those for a science class in school!) The relatively large sizes of the crystal forms at “Nazca” and “Chiu Chiu” are providing clues about the temperature at the time when they grew and the availability of salts and fluids. However, we can’t necessarily assume that the modern-day composition represents the original mineral because sometimes mineral crystals are replaced by other minerals some time after original crystallization. The new minerals are then known as “pseudomorphs” because they have the same shape as the first minerals but not the same composition or molecular structure. item.title: FG kicks off $100m Southeast gas pipeline project
item.description: …As SEDC seals deal with GasSync, commits $3m .. Tinubu says S’East must rise from potential to reality …Mbah, governors hail Tinubu, pledge support for 400km pipeline The Federal Government, through the South East Development Commission (SEDC) has kicked off a $100 million gas distribution pipeline project to boost industrialisation, attract investments and create jobs in the South East. The 400-kilometre pipeline, designed to connect gas resources to industrial and commercial centres across Enugu, Anambra, Imo, Abia and Ebonyi states, has about 150 potential customers identified, with projected demand of 254 million standard cubic feet of gas per day. The investment agreement for the project was signed on Tuesday at the South-East Gas Infrastructure Investment and Project Development Ceremony held at Hotel Presidential, Enugu, marking a significant step towards establishing a regional gas distribution network. Tinubu, represented by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, described the project as a strategic investment that would connect the region’s natural gas resources to industries, strengthen manufacturing and unlock economic opportunities across the five states. “The Southeast’s entrepreneurial spirit is one of Nigeria’s greatest economic assets. I have always believed that the prosperity of the Southeast is inseparable from the prosperity of Nigeria,” the President said. He said the project aligned with his administration’s commitment to building an integrated regional economy, stressing that gas infrastructure should support industrial development across state boundaries rather than serve isolated markets. “Gas infrastructure must therefore serve industries and markets, not stop at political boundaries. That is the economic logic of regional integration,” he said. The President said the pipeline would benefit manufacturers in Aba, strengthen industrial clusters in Nnewi and Onitsha, attract productive enterprises to Enugu, expand agro-processing and manufacturing in Ebonyi and connect Imo’s gas resources to the wider regional economy. He, however, said the ambition extended beyond supplying existing factories to creating the conditions for new industries, industrial parks and investments that had stalled because of unreliable energy supply. “Our ambition is not simply to deliver gas to existing factories. It is to make possible factories that do not yet exist, industrial parks yet to be developed, and investments that have remained on the drawing board because reliable energy was unavailable,” Tinubu said. He described the South-East Development Commission (SEDC) as an institution established to deliver measurable development outcomes, urging it to assess its performance by the investments it mobilised, infrastructure it enabled, opportunities it created and lives it improved. item.title: PANDEF@10: Leaders push for 50% derivation
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA—THE Pan Niger Delta Forum, PANDEF, the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone has called for a total overhaul of the region, demand an increase in the derivation allocation to oil-producing states from the current minimum of 13 percent to 50 percent. It also wants accelerated completion of the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway and urgent environmental remediation across the Niger Delta. PANDEF urged the Federal Government, the Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission, RMAFC, and the National Assembly to initiate measures to raise the allocation to at least 50 percent, just as it argued that the minimum 13 percent derivation allocation had remained unchanged for more than two decades, despite the environmental damage and economic difficulties facing oil-producing communities. Addressing newsmen in Abuja, yesterday, after a meeting of the organisation’s Board of Trustees and National Executive Committee, virtually to mark the 10 years of existence of the organisation, PANDEF National Chairman, Amb. Godknows Igali, said: “The minimum 13 percent derivation allocation had remained unchanged for more than two decades, despite the environmental damage and economic difficulties facing oil-producing communities. We are demanding an upward review to 50 percent. “We also demand the abolition of the onshore/offshore dichotomy in revenue allocation. We insist that offshore oil and gas operations could damage marine ecosystems and fishing grounds relied upon by coastal communities.” The meeting was attended by the Board of Trustees Chairman and former Akwa Ibom State Governor, Obong Victor Attah, former Attorney-General and Minister of Justice, Kanu Agabi, SAN, PANDEF National Publicity Secretary, Minimising Obiuwevbi, alongside political leaders, traditional rulers and other stakeholders from the six South-South states. Further Igali said: “We propose exploring a market-based South-South investment fund to mobilise resources from individuals, businesses, institutions and other stakeholders for investment in critical sectors. The proposed fund would support enterprise development, improve regional connectivity and create jobs, with the organisation planning to engage private-sector players and other partners to develop a workable framework.” On the 2027 elections, he said: “We called on the people of the South-South to exercise their civic responsibilities peacefully and vote according to their conscience, choosing candidates at all levels whose programmes, commitments, and demonstrate capacity align with the aspirations of the region and who can contribute meaningfully to the peace, progress, and development of the Niger Delta. “Also as the country prepares for the elections, we are calling for a framework that extend to environmental remediation to other polluted communities. item.title: Last moments of Katsina cleric, Masussuka
item.description: Family and neighbours of the slain Islamic cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka, have recalled the chain of events preceding his gruesome murder in front of his residence in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, on Monday evening. Masussuka was shot dead alongside his associate, Adamu Abubakar, in an attack claimed by the extremist group Ansaru. The killing has plunged his family, followers and associates into mourning. This is as Amnesty International called on the government to conduct a thorough investigation into the killing and ensure that those responsible were brought to justice. Hours before the incident, at a gathering in his father-in-law’s residence where relatives and well-wishers had assembled to mourn a deceased family member, the cleric had reportedly spoken about the inevitability of death and the need for people to live harmoniously. ‘How my 5 children died in tricycle-tanker crash’ Bangkok’s debt debate: Can Africa secure fairer development finance? Masussuka was said to have reminded the mourners that differences in race, tribe, nationality and social standing should not divide humanity because everyone would eventually return to Allah. A resident, Murtala Narega, who was familiar with the cleric’s final hours, said Masussuka used the gathering at his father-in-law’s residence to remind mourners that differences among people should encourage understanding rather than hostility. “He reminded us that Allah created people differently, but those differences should not be a reason for division or hostility,” Narega said. According to him, the cleric also spoke about the certainty of death, regardless of a person’s wealth, position, or circumstances. “He told us that this world is only a temporary place and that everyone will eventually return to Allah. He advised us to use the time we have to do good and serve humanity,” he said. Narega said the message had become particularly painful following the cleric’s death just hours later. “None of us imagined that we would be mourning him so soon after listening to him speak about death. His words have stayed with us because he reminded us that life is temporary, but we did not know that his own end was so close,” he added. After the gathering, Masussuka reportedly returned to the studio at his residence, where he regularly delivered religious lectures to his followers online. The wife of the late cleric, Hajiya Fatima, recalled that Masussuka had reminded her of the oneness of Allah before he stepped out on the fateful day, adding that shortly afterwards, she heard gunshots. “My husband spoke to me about the oneness of Allah before he left home. Shortly after he left, I heard about four gunshots. Then I received the news that he had been killed,” the widow recounted briefly. “I pray that Allah forgives his shortcomings and grants him Aljannah Firdausi.” The circumstances surrounding the attack have left relatives and associates searching for answers, including whether the assailants knew the cleric

item.title: SK Hynix says memory shortages to persist until 2030
item.description: Korean memory-maker SK Hynix has predicted memory shortages will persist until at least the year 2030 and says that will help it to boost its already exceptional revenue and profits to new levels. In remarks published on Wednesday alongside its quarterly results, the company offered its belief that “a virtuous cycle has taken hold in which AI-driven productivity gains and new revenue generation in areas such as software development, customer service, and search lead to greater AI adoption, which in turn drives increased investment in infrastructure.” SK Hynix thinks this is great news, because it means more buyers are entering the market for AI infrastructure, including “general enterprises” and nations building sovereign infrastructure. In coming years, the company sees even more demand for memory coming from autonomous cars and the growing robotics market. While the company is working hard to build more factories and get them working, execs admitted it can’t do that fast enough to meet demand. “The company assessed that supply … is not keeping pace with the growth of the market,” SK Hynix told investors. “Given technical difficulty of leading-edge processes and the long lead time required to build new production facilities, it expects the structure in which demand exceeds supply to persist through 2030.” It gets worse. SK Hynix has 14 long-term deals with 14 big buyers, who will collectively buy more than half of its output during 2027 and 2028, and some of them want to extend those agreements. The Korean giant doesn’t mind that because the deals include “a mechanism that reflects market conditions within a price range agreed upon with customers” and give it “a structure that secures stable profitability while allowing flexible responses to market changes.” Those deals helped SK Hynix to record quarterly revenue of ₩104.6 trillion ($78.1 billion), up 328 percent year-over-year and 32 percent quarter-over-quarter. Operating profit came in at ₩87.68 trillion ($62.8 billion), up 486 percent year over year. The company told investors it’s not done yet, outlining plans to expand production and emphasize lucrative products that will “scale up revenue and profit one step further next year.” Doing so will likely dent profits elsewhere, because on the company’s earnings call, chief financial officer Kim Woo-hyun predicted “shipment volumes for PCs and mobile devices are expected to decrease due to cost burdens from rising memory prices and supply shortages.” The company also outlined some of its future plans, among them: Increasing HBM4 production, which it believes will “surpass HBM3E in both shipment volume and revenue in the fourth quarter and … establish itself as a mainstream product.” “Rapidly” increasing the portion of its 10nm-class 6th generation (1c) process technology and expand sales of DDR5 and LPDDR5 SOCAMM for AI servers. item.title: The Land of the Standing-Up Rocks
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory The Land of the Standing-Up Rocks Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Some 27 million years ago, a volcano in what’s now southeastern Arizona unleashed a spectacular series of eruptions, strewing more than 1,000 times as much volcanic material across the landscape as Mount St. Helens did in 1980. The explosive eruptions blanketed the region, part of the Chiricahua Apache Nation’s traditional lands, with ash and pumice . Layered into this were massive pyroclastic flows that hardened into deposits of welded rhyolitic tuff that in some areas were nearly 1,600 feet (500 meters) thick, about three times the height of the Washington Monument. As the magma chamber emptied, the ground above it collapsed, leaving a gaping depression—the Turkey Creek caldera —that was roughly 12 miles (19 kilometers) wide and 4,900 feet (1,500 meters) deep. An array of geologic processes, including erosion and weathering , gradually sculpted the welded layer of tuff into the collection of dramatic spires, hoodoos , and canyons that visitors to the caldera area encounter today. The Apache called the area “ The Land of the Standing-Up Rocks ” for good reason. Hiking through Rhyolite Canyon or driving through Bonita Canyon means encountering a dizzying maze of rock pinnacles, some hundreds of feet tall. Others, like Big Balanced Rock , have surprisingly large boulders precariously perched on top. Meanwhile, those at Heart of Rocks and Massai Point are gathered into groups of hundreds. The area was designated a national monument in 1924 to preserve its remarkable geology. In October 2026, it was redesignated as Chiricahua National Park (pronounced cheery-cow-ah ). The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured this cloud-free image of the new national park on July 2, 2026. Individual rock spires are too small to distinguish, but the eroding rhyolitic tuff landscape appears gray. Stream valleys dense with trees and other vegetation, including Rhyolite Canyon and Bonita Canyon, snake across the landscape. With four biogeographic regions converging in the park—the Sonoran Desert, the Chihuahuan Desert, the Rocky Mountains, and the Sierra Madre—it is a haven of plant diversity . Among the 1,000 species growing within the park’s varied desert, grassland, chaparral, deciduous forest, and coniferous forest ecosystems are agaves, prickly pear cacti, yuccas, manzanita, pine, fir, cypress, sycamore, juniper, and oak. As Buffy elegantly puts it: Halloween is “like, dead for the undead.” But 29 years ago, one evildoer decided to wreak havoc in Sunnydale on the one night no one expected. item.title: AI slows growth for Infosys and keeps it afloat at the same time
item.description: Indian tech services giant Infosys has mixed news about AI. In its most recent quarterly results late last week, the company revealed that it’s racked up 29 percent sequential growth in AI revenue, which now delivers 10.5 percent of Infosys’ incoming cash. Those are far nicer numbers than the 1.5 percent year-on-year revenue growth Infosys reported for its second quarter. “Growth was below our expectations. Volume was softer, and price increases were lower than anticipated amid high competitive intensity,” chief financial officer Jayesh Sanghrajka told investors. One reason for lower price increases was that customers expect Infosys to charge less when it uses AI, and those cost savings are now “baked in” to its multi-year deals. CEO and managing director Salil Parekh also pointed to AI as one reason the cost of services is falling. “I think what we see today is there is definitely some of our peers who are putting, I would say, more intense effort into the pricing pressure,” he said, “but it is also across the board because of the environment and also the discussion on AI productivity. If you are talking with clients today on large programs, it is a three or five-year outlook.” That leaves Infosys dependent on new work from AI to boost revenue growth, while AI also makes it hard to keep growing revenue from existing customers. Infosys won’t go low to win deals and intends to hold its margins at around 21 percent, Sanghrajka said. He sought to prove that point by citing “a large deal that we walked out of, or we did not pursue because it did not meet our return expectations.” To help preserve margins, the company is conducting “Project Maximus” to find efficiencies within its own operations. AI-powered tools to win more sales are also in the mix. The company sees difficult months ahead. Sanghrajka said the retail and high-tech industries have slowed their services spending and acknowledged that the second half of Infosys’s financial year is usually its slow period. The company tried to convince investors that they have little to worry about, pointing to $8.8 billion of new deals won in the first half of its financial year – 68 percent of which were net new customers – as a sign that Infosys’ fundamentals are sound. But the company also offered less optimistic guidance about its future. In its Q1 results, Infosys predicted full-year revenue growth of 1.5 to 3.0 percent. In Q2, it revised that prediction to 1.0 to 2.0 percent. Infosys’s share price didn’t dive after that news but is already down over 25 percent in the last twelve months. And Bloomberg reports that investment analysts have downgraded the company, suggesting they feel its prospects are poor. ®

item.title: South Carolina's measles outbreak jumped to Washington state 5 times in 2 weeks
item.description: Since measles was declared eliminated in the US in 2000, the country's occasional cases have come mainly from international travelers—visitors from far-flung places where the virus still spreads freely — or unvaccinated US residents who return from abroad with a highly infectious souvenir. But as vaccination rates have slipped nationwide in recent years and outbreaks grow bigger and more frequent, domestic travel now poses a greater risk than international incursions. In a study published this week in NEJM Evidence, Washington state health officials highlight that risk, detailing how an explosive outbreak in South Carolina reached their distant state through five distinct importation events over two weeks in January. In all, the introductions led to 26 cases among residents before officials stamped out the spread. South Carolina's measles outbreak began on October 2, 2025, and was declared over on April 26, 2026. Officials confirmed 997 cases in the state during the outbreak. At the time, it was the largest measles outbreak recorded since the virus was declared eliminated, but Pennsylvania's ongoing outbreak has since surpassed it. Read full article Comments

item.title: China's top-secret spaceplane can't hide in low-Earth orbit
item.description: A winged Chinese spacecraft bearing a strong resemblance to the US military's X-37B spaceplane was photographed in orbit by a passing US-owned commercial satellite in 2024, and we finally have the image. The Chinese spaceplane has delta wings, payload bay doors, a dark heat shield, and a rear-mounted service module with power-generating solar arrays. In other words, the design of the winged ship is, to a great degree, a copy of the X-37B spaceplane flown by the US Space Force. The photo was taken by a commercial imaging satellite owned by a company called Vantor, known as Maxar in 2024. Vantor is one of several companies that provide reconnaissance imagery of locations around the world to the US military and US intelligence agencies. The same Earth-imaging satellites can point their telescopes at objects in space. Read full article Comments

item.title: FG Approves Six-Month ₦70,000 Transport Support For Workers
item.description: The Federal Government has approved a ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a conciliation meeting with the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). The agreement was reached at a meeting convened by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment in Abuja on Tuesday, October 27, to address issues raised by organised labour. Under the agreement, the government also approved the payment of peculiar allowance arrears, effective from May 1, 2026, with payments scheduled to begin in November in three equal monthly instalments. The parties, however, failed to agree on the effective date for implementing the national minimum wage, although they agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted and begin meeting immediately. The resolutions were contained in a press statement issued by the Ministry of Labour and Employment after the meeting, which was chaired by the Minister, Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, with NLC President Joe Ajaero leading the labour delegation. On the transport intervention, the statement said the Federal Government “will pay a transport intervention of Seventy Thousand Naira (₦70,000) across all levels for a period of six (6) months, commencing from November 2026.” On peculiar allowances, the government approved payments with effect from May 1, 2026, with the arrears to be paid in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. A conciliation meeting between the FG and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). X/@LabourMinNG The statement also addressed outstanding allowances for health workers, stating that “Nineteen (19) months arrears of allowances for health workers will be redeemed within three (3) months with effect from December 2026.” On hazard allowances for agricultural workers, the ministry said the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security had submitted the list of beneficiaries and the cost implications to the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission (NSIWC) for verification. The verification is expected to be completed within two weeks, after which the commission will issue an implementation template. The parties also discussed the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS) adjustment. According to the statement, NSIWC promised to complete the update of the cost implications within three weeks to enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to decide on the adjustment. On tax relief for workers, the statement said the issue would be taken to the National Executive Council because taxation is a statutory matter. The meeting followed an earlier conciliation session held on October 22 and came after discussions on issues raised by the NLC’s Central Working Committee and National Executive Council. item.title: First Israeli Election Exit Polls Show Narrow Edge For Opposition
item.description: The first exit polls from Israel’s elections showed the opposition bloc with a slight edge over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp as voting ended Tuesday, but still shy of an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset. The country’s main pollsters — Channels 11, 12 and 13 — projected the opposition bloc to win 52 or 53 seats, and Netanyahu’s bloc to win 50, although his Likud would be the largest single party in the parliament, with 24 or 25 seats. Israeli Arab parties also made gains after their voter base turned out in high numbers. The exit polls showed the two Arab-majority groupings, Raam and the Joint List, winning 17 or 18 seats between them. In the last election, Likud had walked away with 32 seats, enabling it to cobble together a coalition with smaller far-right parties after Netanyahu’s traditional allies balked at the corruption cases the premier was facing. This time around, those mainstream right-wing parties, by and large, vowed to work with main challenger Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party — projected to nab 21 to 23 seats — to form an opposition coalition capable of unseating Netanyahu. A volunteer stands behind a banner for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party at a polling station in Jerusalem on October 27, 2026, on the day of Israel’s legislative election. Photo by Jewel SAMAD / AFP) “The initial exit poll results indicate a complete lack of confidence in Netanyahu and the October 7 government,” Eisenkot said. Israel’s current opposition chief Yair Lapid said Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a “crushing defeat”, while left-wing leader Yair Golan said the public had “fired the Netanyahu government”. While Raam and the Joint List do not belong to the opposition bloc, they have expressed openness to supporting it. Tuesday’s poll was marked by high turnout, with many voters saying they saw it as pivotal for the country’s future. item.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission 's publication on Monday of Anthropic's S-1 form —ahead of a heavily anticipated initial public offering—has led to plenty of discussion of whether the company's quickly ballooning revenues will be able to overcome its even higher costs. But amid the numbers and forward-looking optimism about AI "rapidly transform[ing] every sector of the global economy in ways greater than the impact of industrialization, electricity, semiconductors, and the internet," Anthropic also spends an inordinate amount of time in its S-1 laying out the myriad risk factors that could bring the company down. Across 93 pages and over 70,000 words, Anthropic's S-1 "Risk Factors" section discusses literally hundreds of potential problems that could negatively impact its business in the coming years. Many of these potential risks are the kind of standard worries about competition, costs, customer acquisition, and potential regulation that almost any business must worry about. But some risks highlight interesting potential points of failure for Anthropic specifically and the hype-filled AI bubble more generally. After wading through Anthropic's book-length treatise on its greatest risks, we've narrowed the list to the seven most surprising, interesting, or thought-provoking potential problems. Consider this a far-from-comprehensive look that potential Anthropic investors should keep in mind. Read full article Comments
